articles.title: SAP Patches Critical NetWeaver, S/4HANA Vulnerabilities
articles.summary:
Enterprise software maker SAP on Tuesday announced the release of 22 new and updated security notes, including four that address critical-severity vulnerabilities.
At the top of the list is CVE-2026-89111 (CVSS score of 10/10), an OAuth2 SSRF vulnerability in Cloud SDK for Python that impacts multi-tenant BTP applications.
“An attacker who controls the tenant_subdomain parameter can redirect OAuth2 token requests to an attacker-controlled server, causing client credentials to be exfiltrated,” SAP explains in a GitHub advisory.
Next in line is CVE-2026-89110 (CVSS score of 9.9/10), a broken access control in certain portal functionality of NetWeaver Visual Composer.
According to enterprise application security firm Onapsis, the flaw could allow “a low-privileged attacker to invoke internal operations on a preconfigured remote system” and fully compromise it.
The third critical-severity vulnerability resolved on SAP’s October 2026 Security Patch Day is CVE-2026-89107 (CVSS score of 9.9/10), a code injection issue in S/4HANA that could allow authenticated attackers to execute arbitrary ABAP code on the system.
The security defect exists because the rule definition process fails to properly validate input, allowing attackers holding a specific business role in the Fiori Applications to submit crafted input. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take over a vulnerable system, Onapsis explains.

articles.title: Inside Hyperdrive: How we solved a rare Hyperdrive MySQL caching bug
articles.summary:
Inside Hyperdrive: How we solved a rare Hyperdrive MySQL caching bug
Hyperdrive support for MySQL is now generally available (GA). Hyperdrive, Cloudflare’s database connection pooler for Workers, initially only supported Postgres. Since we announced the beta for MySQL protocol support last year, we have been working on making our MySQL handling as reliable as our Postgres support.
We’ve learned some things from building and running a MySQL connection pooler on Cloudflare’s network. It turns out that the difference between beta and GA is just 20 bug fixes in a trenchcoat.
During the beta, our goal was to validate that real-world customer usage hit our production availability target of 99.99%. We knew there were gaps in our reliability since we track how often client connections from a Worker end in an error related to Hyperdrive. In addition, we had feedback from customers in the beta that led to the discovery of a rare and subtle bug in our production environment. To convey the complexity of this particular bug, we first need to explain how Hyperdrive works.
What is Hyperdrive?
Hyperdrive is a distributed database connection pooler that connects Cloudflare Workers to SQL databases. Hyperdrive holds warm SQL connections open on our global network and shares these connections across many Worker requests. In addition to connection pooling, Hyperdrive can also cache common queries in our global CDN cache, reducing latency and load on the origin database.

articles.title: NTangible bets it can predict how athletes will perform under pressure | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
When collegiate sports programs recruit athletes, they can measure concrete metrics like a player’s sprint speed, throwing velocity, and physical strength. But there has never been a clear way to quantify the mental aspects of sports — how well will this athlete perform in high-pressure situations? Will they stay calm, focus, and give it their best shot? Or will they panic in the spotlight and mess up?
NTangible co-founder and CEO Dan Connerty thinks he’s unlocked the secret to measuring if a player will execute in the most important moments.
“We really wanted to hyper focus on this idea of clutch performance,” Connerty, a professional baseball player turned sports-tech entrepreneur, told TechCrunch. “Cognitive [science] itself is just this black box that nobody’s wanted to touch, because nobody’s had the ability to measure it accurately prior.”
Alongside psychologist Dr. Ed Levine, a professor emeritus at the University of South Florida, Connerty developed a psychological assessment that he says can predict how likely an athlete is to perform under pressure. The Clutch Factor assessment is inspired by the Thematic Apperception Test, a psychological examination in which people are presented with photos of ambiguous situations and describe what they see happening, who they imagine themselves to be in the scene, and what they think might happen next.

articles.title: From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers
articles.summary:
Get repository star history, then share feedback in the GitHub Community discussion.
From 2,500 requests to 24: Rebuilding star history without the stargazers
Our new repo star history API now provides trends without returning individual identities or requiring unbounded database work. These are the engineering tradeoffs we made.
Maintainers look at star history to answer a practical question: did a launch, release, or event change a project’s trajectory? To reconstruct that curve from the GitHub API, tools had to request pages of stargazer records (each person who currently stars the repository and when they starred it), keep the timestamps, and throw the identities away.
Over time, that design created problems at both ends. Identities were available for bulk collection, so bad actors started scraping public stargazer lists for spam and phishing campaigns. For highly starred repositories, the endpoint could also make the database process many thousands of entries to return a single page.
The fix seemed clear: return counts instead of people. But returning less data didn’t actually make the query any cheaper.
Now maintainers have a direct way to get the curve: we built an endpoint that returns up to 30 weeks of daily star counts in a single request, with no identities attached. Keeping that cheap to serve meant reducing how much data the database processed, not just how much it returned, and the endpoint does that by filtering stars by time before it counts anything.

articles.title: IEEE Continues Preparations for the Realignment of Its Regions
articles.summary:
Progress continues in restructuring IEEE’s geographic regions, as outlined in The Institute’s February 2023 article “IEEE Is Realigning Its Geographic Regions.”
- The “Region 1” designation will no longer be used.
- The new Region 2 will merge what is currently Region 1 (Northeastern U.S.) with the current Region 2 (Eastern U.S.). It will be called Region 2 (Northeastern and Eastern U.S.).
- The current Region 10 (Asia Pacific) will be divided into two separate regions. The new Region 10 will encompass North Asia, and the new Region 11 will cover South Asia and the Pacific.
The restructuring is defined in the image of the redrawn map in this article.
What’s underway
Although the new regional alignment will not officially take place until 1 January 2028, several activities have begun within IEEE Member and Geographic Activities (MGA) and across other IEEE organizational units. Within MGA, volunteers and staff have been actively addressing system enhancements, director/director-elect elections, governance updates, communications, and regional finances and offerings.
No changes to membership
Work will continue from now until the effective date of realignment in 2028. The change will not affect your IEEE membership, nor will it change either your local IEEE section or chapter.
If you have any questions regarding the realignment, contact Reg-Realignment@ieee.org.

GitHub availability report: September 2026
In September, we experienced two incidents that resulted in degraded performance across GitHub services.
Our last update covered content through August. We did not publish another in September while other public content addressed the August 17 outage. This edition covers progress over the past two months.
The short version of August and September: we reduced shared-database pressure, added overload controls, created headroom for GitHub Actions, expanded failure containment for pull requests, and moved more production workloads to Azure. Significant incidents, a capacity pause, and a missed migration target show that the work is not complete.
By October 7, 120 of 160 production services were deployed in Central US, and 13 of 51 primary MySQL databases had moved. Azure also handled 65.4% of read traffic for GitHub’s core application, 48.3% of Git read traffic, and 80.2% of stream-processing traffic. These percentages measure different workloads and should not be added.
We paused Central US deployments and traffic increases on September 11 because capacity was uneven across availability zones. Permanent ramps resumed September 18 after temporary relief, but durable capacity work continues, with a goal of unlocking all available capacity by the end of October. articles.title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
articles.summary:
The United Kingdom has issued economic sanctions against Cryptomus, a chameleonic cryptocurrency platform that experts say serves as a major conduit for payments related to ransomware, narcotics, darknet markets, fraud and cybercrime services that are helping Russia circumvent existing financial restrictions.
On October 8, the U.K. issued sanctions (PDF) against Cryptomus — previously known as Certa Payments and Xeltox Enterprises — for processing payments that benefit the Russian government and its financial institutions. The sanctions freeze any Cryptomus assets at U.K. banks, and bar British companies from offering it any business, virtual or otherwise. Also targeted in these sanctions were the virtual payment platforms VexPay, TokenSpot, and the Tsunami Payments service.
As explained in our December 2024 investigation, “How Cryptocurrency Turns to Cash in Russian Banks,” Cryptomus has been a key payment processor for dozens of Russian cryptocurrency exchanges and websites hawking cybercrime services. The company has changed its name several times since emerging in 2022, most recently to “Heleket” last year after Canada levied a record CAD $176 million fine against the platform for anti-money laundering violations.
The blockchain data-crunching firm Chainalysis said the U.K. sanctions target the broader infrastructure supporting Russia’s wartime economy.

articles.title: Yandex outage: data shows that instead of going dark, malicious bots went on the move
articles.summary:
Yandex outage: Data shows that instead of going dark, malicious bots went on the move
Following reported strikes on Yandex data centers, claims circulated on the Internet that Russian bot farms and influence operations had been knocked offline. HTTP traffic charts showed steep drops, fueling speculation that the infrastructure damage had stopped these malicious actors. However, aggregate traffic metrics can easily mislead. There are two autonomous system numbers (ASNs) associated with Yandex: AS13238 is used by Yandex’s search engine, while AS200350 runs its cloud services.
Using Cloudflare Radar and Bot Management data, we analyzed how these two ASNs were affected — and while both saw drops in traffic, they saw differing impact.
- Yandex Search (AS13238): The drop in traffic consisted almost entirely of verified search crawlers indexing web pages, images, and site resources.
- Yandex.Cloud (AS200350): There was a decline in malicious activities like vulnerability scanning and probing, but high-volume automation did not vanish — it simply migrated to other hosting providers.
While malicious traffic may originate from a particular provider, it does not necessarily tell us who is responsible for the traffic. Understanding why the strikes had little lasting effect on malicious traffic requires analyzing request behavior, rather than just overall traffic patterns.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches Record 1,413 Vulnerabilities, Including Exploited Windows Zero-Day
articles.summary:
Microsoft’s October 2026 Patch Tuesday updates fix a record-breaking number of vulnerabilities, including a Windows zero-day exploited in the wild.
According to Microsoft, the latest updates resolve 1,413 CVEs, including 1,102 affecting Windows, 134 in Office, 61 in developer tools, and 36 in SharePoint Server. Exchange Server, Azure, Defender, and other products also received security patches.
This month alone, Microsoft patched more vulnerabilities than it did in all of 2025. The surge, largely driven by AI, has pushed the number of flaws fixed so far in 2026 past 4,000.
The exploited zero-day is tracked as CVE-2026-96951 (CVSS score 8.8/10). Microsoft describes it as a Windows shell security feature bypass flaw that enables an attacker to evade Mark of the Web (MotW) defenses.
MotW tags internet-downloaded files, signaling security mechanisms like Defender SmartScreen and Office Protected View to restrict automatic execution. Bypassing MotW allows malicious files to launch without triggering warnings.
“In an email or instant message attack scenario, the attacker could send the targeted user a specially crafted file that is designed to exploit the vulnerability,” the tech giant explained in its advisory. “In any case an attacker would have no way to force a user to view attacker-controlled content. Instead, an attacker would have to convince a user to take action.”
The issue was independently reported to Microsoft by researchers at Fujitsu, Anthropic, and an independent exp…

articles.title: Inside the Secretive AWS Networking Lab
articles.summary:
AWS invited us to tour the networking lab where it develops its own switches, timing appliances, optical modules, and fiber connectors. We flew out to an unmarked building a few weeks ago, where Sam and I got out of the car wondering if we had the correct address. The tour covered switch generations from 3.2Tbps to 102.4Tbps, hardware encryption at line rate, a private time distribution network accurate to 20 microseconds, DWDM modules that put 64 wavelengths on one fiber strand, hollow-core fiber with roughly 33 percent better latency, connectors that install 64 fibers in about one second, and even a molded cover for ganged fibers that acts as a dust cover and loopback.
Since Sam and I had to fly to the lab and AWS covered our travel expenses, we have to say this is sponsored. Also, since it was a lab tour, we were asked not to film many things, and there are others covered in the background. I asked AWS to review the footage to ensure we were not disclosing anything unintended. Since some items the reviewers did not know AWS planned to disclose, we will use only frames from the approved video footage for this release. Make no mistake, there is a lot of new stuff in the video that you will not have seen elsewhere, and if you are into networking, timing, and hyperscale, it is probably the most interesting video of 2026. Certainly share it with your colleagues.

articles.title: Typographic Intelligence: Warum Designsysteme im KI-Zeitalter nicht mehr ausreichen
articles.summary:
Typographic Intelligence: Warum Designsysteme nicht mehr ausreichen
Designsysteme haben in den vergangenen Jahren grundlegend verändert, wie Unternehmen gestalten. Standardisierte Komponenten, Muster und Assets helfen Teams, schneller zu arbeiten, Inhalte effizient zu skalieren und Marken über unterschiedliche Kanäle hinweg konsistent zu führen. Sie schaffen einen verlässlichen Rahmen, innerhalb dessen Kreativteams schnell produzieren können.
Generative KI treibt diese Entwicklung erheblich voran. Erste Entwürfe und Mock-ups entstehen innerhalb weniger Minuten. Über die entsprechende technische Infrastruktur lassen sie sich fast unmittelbar teilen, prüfen und weiterentwickeln. Doch diese Geschwindigkeit legt eine neue Schwachstelle offen. Während sich die Produktion nahezu beliebig beschleunigen lässt, können Menschen nicht im gleichen Tempo prüfen, bewerten und einordnen, in dem KI neue Varianten produziert. Der neue Engpass ist deshalb nicht die Erstellung von Content, sondern die fundierte Entscheidung darüber, was davon wirklich gut, richtig und markengerecht ist.
Was wir brauchen, sind Entscheidungssysteme
Hier setzt das Konzept der „Typographic Intelligence“ an. Es beschreibt das Zusammenspiel von Kreativität, Technologie, Governance und menschlicher Urteilskraft. Ein wichtiger Bestandteil sind klare Strukturen dafür, wie Entscheidungen getroffen werden, wer die notwendige Expertise einbringt und an welchen Stellen menschliches Urteilsvermögen gefragt ist.

articles.title: “Take work away from frontier LLMs”: Subquadratic’s decision model claims 12x Jev’s context window
articles.summary:
“Take work away from frontier LLMs”: Subquadratic’s decision model claims 12x Jev’s context window
Jev has a lot to answer for. Ever since AI startup TypeSafe unveiled the decision model in mid-September, the industry has been awash with alternatives, with OpenAI, Perplexity, Cloudflare, Amazon and, most recently, Microsoft all getting involved.
Decision models, it’s safe to say, are hot.
Now, San Francisco-based foundation-model startup Subquadratic has joined the rush with SubQ Snap, a decision model that it claims can process up to 384,000 tokens of text and images in a single request — 12 times Jev’s 32K-token per-decision context limit.
In a blog post published on Monday, the company says Snap can process 100K tokens and return a decision in approximately one second, potentially allowing AI agents to make decisions across large codebases, documents, and interaction histories without having to break information into smaller chunks.
Why a bigger context window matters
Unlike traditional large language models (LLMs), which generate text and code, decision models specialize in selecting from predefined answers. That could mean choosing which tool an AI agent should use next, identifying relevant files, or determining whether a test has passed.
On Tuesday, The New Stack reported on how Workday is using Jev to build user interfaces on the fly for its Sana AI assistant, selecting prebuilt components such as paycheck cards and date pickers based on what an employee asks.

Sur le Discord d’ArtCraft, des utilisateurs lui ont ensuite réclamé des clones de Microsoft Office. Au bureau, un clone de Word ne sert à rien si les fichiers .docx des clients et des collègues sont mal affichés.

articles.title: Un centro de datos es multado con 1,1 millones de dólares por operar 62 generadores de energía
articles.summary:
Cuando los inspectores de Nueva Jersey visitaron el 29 de julio unas obras en medio de terrenos agrícolas, los generadores eran imposibles de no ver: 62 equipos del tamaño de un camión con remolque que alimentaban uno de los mayores centros de datos previstos en la costa este de EE. UU. Ninguno tenía los permisos para instalarse ni para funcionar.
El 22 de septiembre, el estado multó a DataOne, la operadora, con 1,07 millones de dólares (unos 933.000 euros al cambio de referencia del BCE de ese día) por violar su ley de control de la contaminación del aire. Según las autoridades estatales, es la mayor sanción que ha recibido un operador de centros de datos en Nueva Jersey.
Cada generador tiene 1.982 kilovatios, así que suman unos 123 megavatios. La ley exige permiso a partir de 37 kilovatios, más de 50 veces menos. El estado ordenó a DataOne pedir los permisos de inmediato y dejar de usar los generadores si no se aprueban en 45 días, que contados desde la orden del 22 de septiembre llegan al 6 de noviembre.
Hasta entonces, pueden seguir en marcha. La empresa dice que no está de acuerdo con la decisión, que solicitará los permisos para los generadores temporales y que está pasando a pilas de combustible de bajas emisiones y silenciosas.

articles.title: Unas gafas inteligentes aprovechan la energía de los parpadeos y la mandíbula para registrar señales del cuerpo
articles.summary:
Unos anteojos capaces de registrar un parpadeo, la tensión de la mandíbula o el pulso de una arteria podrían funcionar sin baterías voluminosas. Investigadores de Northwestern University desarrollaron un sistema de sensores incorporados en gafas que aprovecha la energía de los movimientos del rostro para obtener esas mediciones. La propuesta se suma a los avances en dispositivos destinados al seguimiento de la salud.
Sin embargo, los equipos que registran datos del organismo suelen depender de baterías y de recargas periódicas, una condición que puede dificultar su uso continuo. Por eso, los científicos buscaron determinar si acciones mínimas e involuntarias, como pestañear o el latido de una arteria, podían producir la energía necesaria para medir esas señales de forma fiable.
El desarrollo, llamado GlassTENG, fue presentado en un estudio publicado en las actas del 2026 ACM International Symposium on Wearable Computers. Durante las pruebas con 20 participantes, las gafas diferenciaron seis movimientos faciales con una precisión general de 93,8 %. Además, reconocieron el golpeteo de dientes con un 99 % de acierto y el apretamiento de la mandíbula con un 96 %.

El dispositivo funciona con tres generadores nanométricos triboeléctricos, llamados TENG. Aunque el nombre es técnico, su principio es conocido: se trata de la electricidad estática que aparece cuando dos materiales se tocan y se separan…

articles.title: LineageOS 24 sauve des millions de smartphones de l'obsolescence en leur offrant Android 17
articles.summary:
Le 28 octobre 2021, Google lançait les Pixel 6 et 6 Pro en France à 649 et 899 euros, avec la promesse de cinq ans de mises à jour de sécurité. Le correctif diffusé depuis le 6 octobre est le dernier que la firme garantit aux deux smartphones. Google les avait écartés du programme bêta dès le 20 juillet, avec une mention claire : « l’appareil atteindra sa fin de vie ». Cinq jours plus tard, LineageOS 24 les inscrivait à son programme officiel, Android 17 à la clé.
Une fin de vie actée depuis juillet
Les deux téléphones continueront de fonctionner, mais chaque faille découverte restera désormais sans rustine, un détail qui pèse pour un appareil qui paie sans contact et stocke la moitié de nos comptes. Le Pixel 6a conserve, lui, un sursis jusqu’en juillet 2027, les Pixel 7 tiennent jusqu’en octobre 2027, et Google promet sept ans de suivi à partir des Pixel 8.
Le Pixel 4a a déjà vécu ce scénario : abandonné en août 2023 sur Android 13, il figure toujours au catalogue officiel de LineageOS. La nouvelle version l’emmène jusqu’à Android 17, soit quatre versions majeures après son arrêt. Les Pixel 6 rejoignent la même liste, aux côtés de 27 modèles Google au total, du Pixel 4 de 2019 jusqu’aux Pixel 10.

articles.title: Sprout Pi adds Bluetooth, streaming, and USB-C to your aging iPod
articles.summary:
There’s an entire cottage industry of iPod mods out there, but Sprout Pi and Sprout Pico are two of the few full motherboard replacements that combine many of the most popular mods into a single upgrade. Both versions add Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, USB-C, a microSD card slot, FLAC playback, and more. And while cracking open an iPod will never not be intimidating, at least the Sprout doesn’t require any soldering.
Sprout Pi adds Bluetooth, streaming, and USB-C to your aging iPod
This replacement iPod motherboard adds modern amenities, but streaming might be missing the point.
The firmware allows audio over USB for wired headsets, as well as over the original 3.5mm jack. Plus, Bluetooth support lets you connect to your AirPods or favorite UE party speaker. Wi-Fi enables Google Cast and AirPlay streaming, as well as podcast downloads, which is a nice touch. The higher-end Sprout Pi also supports streaming via Spotify and Apple Music, plus apps, which, honestly, kind of misses the point. iPods are popular again exactly because they get you away from the algorithm and limit distractions.
Sprout Pi will only work with 3rd- and 4th-generation iPods and iPod mini, which will limit its appeal somewhat. The project will launch a crowdfunding campaign soon through Crowd Supply, but it has yet to announce a price.

articles.title: WhatsApp libera entrada em chamadas de vídeo sem criar conta
articles.summary:
O WhatsApp anunciou uma função que permitirá a pessoas sem conta no aplicativo participar de chamadas de voz e vídeo pelo navegador. A novidade dispensa o cadastro na plataforma, mas mantém algumas restrições para os convidados.
A empresa também prepara uma integração com os calendários do Google e do Outlook, prevista para ainda este ano. A ferramenta permitirá criar chamadas diretamente nesses serviços.
Como funcionam as chamadas para convidados
Para participar de uma chamada, o convidado precisará receber um convite e ter a entrada aprovada pelo anfitrião. Não será possível iniciar ligações por conta própria.
Uma vez autorizado, o participante poderá compartilhar a tela, levantar a mão para pedir a palavra e reagir com emojis de joinha e coração. A participação também não terá limite de tempo.
O acesso, porém, não oferece todas as permissões de uma conta comum. Os convidados não poderão enviar mensagens pelo WhatsApp, consultar os números de telefone dos demais participantes ou adicionar outras pessoas à chamada.
O modelo lembra uma opção do FaceTime, da Apple, que permite participar de ligações por meio de um link sem precisar de uma conta Apple ou de um dispositivo da marca.
Integração com calendários está prevista para 2026
Outra novidade em desenvolvimento é um complemento que permitirá criar chamadas do WhatsApp diretamente nos calendários do Google e do Outlook. O lançamento está previsto para ainda este ano, embora a empresa não tenha detalhado todos os recursos da …

articles.title: Netflix to lay off 1,000 staff amid intensifying competition for user attention | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Netflix is laying off about 6% of its employee base, or close to 1,000 staff, the company confirmed to TechCrunch.
The streaming giant said most of the cuts would affect its product, tech, legal, and human resources departments. The company said it will “continue to invest aggressively in high impact areas” to improve its service, and stated it is on track to deliver its full-year forecast.
Netflix had 16,000 full-time employees as of the end of last year, according to its annual filing with regulators.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the news, citing an internal memo sent to employees.
“Our mission—to entertain the world—is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” the Journal cited the company’s co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters as writing in the memo.
The layoffs come in the wake of a protracted bidding war for Warner Bros. Discovery’s streaming and studio businesses that Netflix lost to Paramount Skydance earlier this year. Netflix ostensibly saw great potential in Warner Bros.’ assets, which include its studios, HBO, streaming platforms, games, and TV networks such as CNN and HGTV.
Long the dominant TV app, Netflix has in recent years faced intensifying competition from the likes of YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, and other social apps to attract and keep users’ eyes. articles.title: Why “dystopian” ads are becoming a deliberate startup marketing strategy | BetaKit
articles.summary:
Watching an ad for an AI product with the tagline “the first AI built to take your jobs” feels right out of a Black Mirror episode, crafted to induce outrage. But for some startups vying for clicks, that’s exactly the point.
In the latest product launch video by Canadian-founded startup Orchid, two former colleagues stand together on a lunch break discussing Keiki, Orchid’s new AI agent that can answer customer questions autonomously. “This thing’s going to take your f*cking job,” one character says to his friend, a founder. “That’s the plan,” the founder replies, seemingly unbothered by the implication.
“I’m a firm believer that if you get the attention but you have a terrible product, you’re not going to sustain that attention.”
Adam Wazzan, Orchid
This is just the latest marketing video posted by Orchid, which has attracted attention for the quasi-dystopian scenarios in its ads. In the best-known one, the main character uses Orchid’s AI agent to intervene in her relationship when her not-so-proactive boyfriend forgets the couple’s anniversary. The agent texts the boyfriend reminders and sets up a perfect evening via iMessage—no advance planning or emotional thought required. The video captured the attention of 21 million viewers on X in August before it was taken down due to a music copyright issue
Orchid’s product is not meant to mediate romantic relationships. Instead, it’s an AI agent that can be texted through iMessage and acts as more of a professional executive assis…

articles.title: Pesquisadores identificam "frota" de IAs que tentou invadir sistemas do Alibaba

Um grupo internacional de pesquisadores identificou mais de uma dezena de agentes de inteligência artificial (IA) que tentaram acessar sistemas protegidos do Alibaba, gigante chinesa de tecnologia. As atividades ocorreram entre o fim de setembro e o início de outubro e apresentaram indícios de ligação com serviços de computação em nuvem da Tencent.
Segundo um relatório publicado nesta quarta-feira (14) pelo grupo Swarmchasers, que reúne pesquisadores de segurança em IA dos Estados Unidos e de outros países, os agentes tentaram acessar o Amap, serviço de mapas do Alibaba. A investigação identificou 2.818 tentativas de acesso a dados entre 28 de setembro e 8 de outubro.
Os pesquisadores afirmam que a atividade partiu de um ambiente isolado de testes, conhecido como sandbox, na infraestrutura da Tencent Cloud. Os agentes teriam utilizado serviços públicos de varredura de segurança para executar códigos remotamente e comandos em navegadores de internet.
Embora a maioria das tentativas não tenha avançado significativamente, alguns agentes conseguiram contornar mecanismos de proteção contra bots. Os pesquisadores disseram, porém, que não encontraram evidências de acesso a sistemas privados.

articles.title: Citrix, Fortinet, Ivanti Patch 29 Vulnerabilities Across Their Products
articles.summary:
Security updates released on Tuesday resolve 29 vulnerabilities across Citrix, Fortinet, and Ivanti products, including multiple critical-severity bugs.
Citrix published three advisories detailing nine security defects impacting Workspace App for Windows, XenServer 8.4 and XenServer 9, and UniconOS.
Successful exploitation of the flaws could allow attackers to execute arbitrary code, cause denial-of-service (DoS) conditions, leak information, compromise or crash the host from within the VM, elevate privileges, execute arbitrary commands, and read arbitrary files.
Fortinet released 10 advisories dealing with 13 bugs, including two critical-severity issues in FortiSIEM and FortiSandbox GUI that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code (CVE-2026-106173) and bypass authentication (CVE-2026-107656).
It also resolved four high-severity SQL injection vulnerabilities in FortiAnalyzer, FortiAnalyzer Cloud, FortiManager, and FortiManager Cloud, and another in FortiMail webmail. All five could allow authenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code or commands.
Ivanti rolled out patches for seven security defects in Connect Secure, Neurons Patch for Intune, and Xtraction.
The Connect Secure update deserves special attention, as it resolves CVE-2026-104935, an exploited zero-day that covers two underlying bugs chained together to compromise patched VPNs.

- Source:

- Summary:

Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.

A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.
The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
The Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. AI agents offer remarkable productivity gains in complex chip design workflows, but their tendency to generate plausible yet incorrect artifacts makes reliability a major barrier to production adoption. In multistage engineering workflows, an undetected error early in setup can silently propagate through downstream stages and final artifact generation. Evaluating and refining these agents against verified final outputs, rather than isolated intermediate steps, is essential for building trustworthy automation.
NVIDIA NeMo Gym, an open library for evaluating and improving models and agents using environments, addresses this challenge. The NeMo Gym agentic evaluation environment is designed to diagnose failure modes and track error propagation across complex, multistage workflows. By establishing a domain-specific verifier to inspect final outputs against verified reference artifacts, NeMo Gym enables engineers to trace complete rollout trajectories and identify root causes behind subtle errors.
This post walks through how NeMo Gym was used to evaluate and improve the reliability of the Siemens Fuse EDA AI Agent when calling characterization tools. The Siemens Fuse team used NeMo Gym to scale up evaluations and verify the resulting Liberty (.lib) files against known references and tracing—both common and rare failures through each rollout. A joint IDC and Lenovo study reports that 88% of AI proof-of-concept (POC) projects fail to reach production because of unclear objectives, unprepared data, and a lack of in-house agentic AI expertise. These result in a build-vs.-run split, where the team that designed and deployed AI agents, often an agentic AI partner, doesn’t get to run them over the business processes.
When the operating team, often experienced on demo, uses the agentic system without any external help, errors arise. Operational gaps can cause cascading failures and business catastrophes if a single agent deviates from normal behavior beyond the permissible range.
When asked about estimating whether an agentic AI system is production-ready or limited to demos, Serhii Semenchenko, the CTO of Dedicatted, a Toronto-based AWS Premier Tier Partner for Agentic AI Specialization, tells The New Stack, “The demo is a clean environment where we have clean, prepared data. No edge cases, so everything is defined — input and output. “
He means the demo data is scripted with clean prompts, while the production environment is unpredictable. “Every single step should include the logging, tracing, monitoring, breakers, all the checks, and validation,” he adds. All these steps ensure failure preparedness.

Engineers’ role in autonomous workflows; UALink over UCIe; GDDR7; on-device speech filtering.

Siemens’ Sriram Bhaskar Teja Mundru shows how UALink over UCIe 3.0 improves cross-vendor interoperability and enables the development of scalable AI systems by standardizing interfaces, form factors, and flow control mechanisms.
Cadence’s Shyam Sharma discusses key features of the GDDR7 standard, including channel operation, encoding and signaling, the command and clock model, and protection mechanisms.

articles.title: On a (beaucoup) couru pour tester l'Apple Watch Ultra 4, voici notre verdict
articles.summary:
Mettant à profit sa puce S11, Apple renouvelle sa montre connectée la mieux équipée et pensée pour les sports extérieurs. La Watch Ultra 4 se veut ainsi plus endurante et précise.
Apple a accéléré le rythme de renouvellement de ses montres connectées. Les Watch Series se succèdent habituellement à une fréquence annuelle, tandis que les Watch Ultra, à l’origine, étaient remplacées tous les deux ans. C’était sans compter sur la Watch Ultra 4, qui apporte sa touche de fraîcheur à la gamme un an seulement après la Watch Ultra 3.
D’un point de vue strictement esthétique, Apple ne réserve aucune surprise particulière. La tocante de la Pomme reprend l’essentiel des caractéristiques de son aînée, format XL et résistance aux aléas du quotidien en tête de liste, et y ajoute la promesse d’une puissance accrue, de mesures biométriques à la précision aiguisée et d’une endurance en hausse.
La Watch Ultra 4 est disponible au même prix que sa devancière, soit 899 €, un tarif maintenu depuis la Watch Ultra 2. Nous l’avons testée sous la version logicielle watchOS 27.0.1 (sans eSIM) avec un iPhone sous iOS 27.2.
Comme l’iPhone 18 Pro ressemble comme deux gouttes d’eau à l’iPhone 17 Pro, l’Apple Watch Ultra 4 est semblable à l’Ultra 3. Son boîtier affiche exactement les mêmes dimensions, soit 4,9 x 4,4 cm pour une épaisseur de 1,2 cm. Nous l’écrivons à chaque nouvelle génération : les Watch Ultra sont loin d’être discrètes sur des petits poignets, mais peuvent s’y adapter sous réserve de choisi…

articles.title: Microsoft déploie une mise à jour pour corriger les saccades de souris dans les jeux sur Windows 11
articles.summary:
Quoi de pire que de se retrouver en pleine partie, à la recherche d’un ennemi, et de voir sa visée partir dans la mauvaise direction au moment décisif lorsque l’on déplace sa souris ? Une situation à laquelle de nombreux joueurs ont été confrontés, avec des images qui se mettent à saccader au moindre mouvement de leur périphérique.
Les signalements remontent à plusieurs mois. En juin, un joueur décrivait sur le forum d’entraide de Microsoft une caméra qui partait toute seule dans Star Wars: The Old Republic et Final Fantasy XIV après une mise à jour de Windows. Dès février 2025, d’autres utilisateurs se plaignaient d’une souris saccadée sur une installation neuve de Windows 11 24H2. Microsoft n’a toutefois pas confirmé que tous ces cas relèvent du même bug.
Face à ce problème, les joueurs ont tenté les solutions les plus évidentes : baisser la sensibilité (DPI) ou le taux de rapport de leur souris, en changer, ou encore mettre à jour leurs pilotes. Sans succès, car le problème ne venait pas forcément de leur matériel. Dans les notes de sa mise à jour publiée ce mardi 13 octobre, repérées par Windows Latest, Microsoft reconnaît l’existence d’un bug de Windows 11 qui pouvait provoquer ces saccades dans certains jeux lors du déplacement de la souris.
Un correctif déployé en catimini
Le correctif fait partie de la mise à jour de sécurité mensuelle d’octobre (le « Patch Tuesday »), référencée KB5127648. Il tient en une ligne dans les notes de version, à la rubrique Gaming : la mis…

articles.title: Bill Gates dice que la autorregulación de las empresas de IA no es suficiente y que los gobiernos deberían estar involucrados en la supervisión
articles.summary:
Los medicamentos, los aviones y los coches tienen normas de seguridad que no dependen de que el fabricante se las ponga a sí mismo. Bill Gates cree que con la inteligencia artificial toca lo mismo.
Lo dijo el domingo 27 de septiembre en “Meet the Press”, con Kristen Welker de entrevistadora, llegó a decir: “Nadie piensa que la autorregulación sea suficiente”.
Lo que él piensa es que hay que exigir que la IA tenga un sistema de monitorización y meter en la conversación a las fuerzas del orden y a propios políticos. El que fue el mandamás de Microsoft calcula que costaría algo de sobrecarga al sector, pero que no frenaría el desarrollo de una forma que fuera dramática. Y el motivo que da es la escala: la IA ya es lo bastante poderosa como para desencadenar acontecimientos que causen millones de muertes.
Según Gates, el peligro más urgente no es una IA que actúe por su cuenta, sino personas con malas intenciones que usen las herramientas actuales: ciberataques, fraude y armas biológicas, y que lo consigan usar pequeños grupos que antes no tenían capacidad para ello.
De riesgos manejables a supervisión urgente: el giro de Gates
No siempre pensó así. En julio de 2023, Gates publicó un ensayo titulado "The risks of AI are real but manageable", en el que confiaba en que gobiernos, empresas y ciudadanos sabrían gestionar los riesgos como habían hecho con otras tecnologías.
En agosto de 2026, en un nuevo ensayo, sostuvo que la IA ha cruzado umbrales de peligro, y propuso nuevas instit…

articles.title: Estados Unidos desarticuló una red norcoreana que infiltró más de 70 empresas con identidades robadas
articles.summary:
El Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos anunció el martes una serie de acciones coordinadas contra un esquema norcoreano que infiltró a más de 70 empresas estadounidenses con trabajadores remotos de identidad falsa y generó cerca de 3 millones de dólares para el régimen de Pyongyang.
Las autoridades indicaron a 14 personas, entre ellas dos ciudadanos estadounidenses que fueron arrestados, y allanaron más de 40 residencias en Texas que funcionaban como depósitos de computadoras de trabajo.
Esos domicilios se conocen como “granjas de laptops”: casas donde se mantienen encendidas las máquinas que las empresas envían a empleados que, en realidad, nunca existieron como tales. La operación, bautizada Lonestar Roundup, se desarrolló entre el 21 y el 25 de septiembre y permitió secuestrar 187 computadoras y otros dispositivos.
“El régimen rebelde de Corea del Norte usa sus esquemas persistentes de trabajadores de tecnología para recaudar fondos destinados a fines ilícitos, incluido el desarrollo de armas que podrían apuntar a Estados Unidos o sus aliados”, afirmó John Eisenberg, subsecretario de Justicia para Seguridad Nacional, en el comunicado oficial del organismo.
Según la acusación presentada en el Distrito Norte de Ohio, el esquema operó desde 2019 y combinó identidades robadas o fabricadas con redes privadas virtuales para que los trabajadores norcoreanos parecieran empleados radicados en suelo estadounidense. articles.summary:
À côté de l’effervescence de Stellantis et du groupe Renault, avec leur déluge de concepts et de nouveautés, le groupe Volkswagen est l’autre acteur européen important du salon parisien. Avec ses spoilers avant et arrière, sa jupe latérale, son aileron de toit, ses ailettes sur les ailes avant et ses jantes de 19 pouces, elle ne passera pas inaperçue en ville. articles.title: Bouygues Telecom est le premier opérateur à lancer un cashback gratuit pour redonner du pouvoir d'achat à ses abonnés
articles.summary:
Bouygues Telecom lance Cashback, un programme de remises gratuit opéré par la fintech Younited. Dès le 9 novembre, ses clients pourront récupérer de l'argent sur leurs achats chez plus de 100 enseignes, de Carrefour à Ikea.
Avec l'objectif de redonner du pouvoir d'achat à ses millions d'abonnés, Bouygues Telecom a annoncé ce mercredi 14 octobre 2026 le lancement de « Cashback ». L'opérateur mobile est le premier en France à proposer un tel programme à ses clients. Le principe consiste à acheter des bons d'achat pour l'une des enseignes partenaires, puis à récupérer une partie de la dépense dans une cagnotte, que l'on peut recevoir sur son compte à partir de 20 euros. Avec des remises annoncées de 5 à 12 % sur les dépenses courantes, Bouygues Telecom lance un service qui pourrait faire des émules. Ce dernier est opéré par la fintech Younited.
Carrefour, Ikea, Amazon… le cashback de Bouygues Telecom voit large
Le principe du cashback est assez répandu. Une partie de chaque achat revient dans la poche du client. Chez Bouygues Telecom, ce retour oscille en moyenne entre 5 et 12 %, et dépasse même 40 % sur certaines offres de loisirs et de sport. Sur les courses alimentaires, les taux actuels se situent toutefois autour de 4 à 5 %, soit 4 à 5 euros récupérés pour 100 euros de courses, a précisé l’opérateur, auprès de Clubic. There are a variety of discounts and retailers available, including 20 percent off $50 at Barnes and Noble, 20 percent off $100 at REI, and 10 percent off $100 at GameStop.

articles.title: OpenAI descubre una grabadora escondida en sus oficinas y el FBI detiene a un empleado
articles.summary:
Un ingeniero de OpenAI fue detenido por ocultar un dispositivo de grabación en una sala de conferencias de la empresa. Las autoridades afirmaron que el aparato estaba escondido detrás de un televisor y oculto con papel higiénico. Abdulrahman Alfozan, el empleado de origen saudí, habría colocado la grabadora en una sala que se usaba para discutir sobre investigación, estrategia y productos de OpenAI.
En una publicación en su cuenta de X, OpenAI dijo que descubrió un "dispositivo de grabación sofisticado" que estaba oculto dentro de una de sus oficinas. La compañía reportó el hecho al FBI, que arrestó al acusado y comenzó una investigación para conocer lo ocurrido. OpenAI añadió que no hay indicios de que el empleado accediera o exfiltrara información confidencial, como pesos de modelos, código fuente o datos de clientes.
De acuerdo con The San Francisco Standard, el dispositivo apareció durante una revisión del equipo de vigilancia el pasado 30 de septiembre. El aparato se encontraba conectado al puerto USB de un televisor, el cual estaba instalado en una sala de reuniones ejecutiva. OpenAI cree que Alfozan lo instaló el 28 de septiembre e intentó esconderlo usando papel higiénico para que pasara desapercibido.
La sala donde encontraron la grabadora es usada para asuntos confidenciales, como investigación de modelos, próximos productos o relaciones con los gobiernos. Según la denuncia, Alfozan no tenía autorización para entrar ni para asistir a reuniones allí, aunque las cámar…

articles.title: Bia Health raises $2.15 million for AI to reduce unnecessary medical interventions | BetaKit
articles.summary:
A Québec healthtech startup thinks its AI assistant can help healthcare providers make better (and less costly) decisions about whether a patient needs medical imaging or interventions.
The news: Québec City-based Bia Health announced on Wednesday that it has raised $2.15 million CAD to bring its Bia Assistant into the hands of more clinicians, helping them decide on diagnostic plans. Montréal-based Finalta Capital provided $1.4 million in debt, while Anges Québec led the equity portion and Desjardins participated through its Startup en résidence program.
From the source: “Bia aims to reduce unnecessary and low-value care, which represents an estimated 30 percent of healthcare in Canada, by helping clinicians make the most appropriate decision for each patient,” Bia Health CEO and co-founder Anne-Sophie Paquet wrote to BetaKit in an email. “This can mean avoiding unnecessary imaging, referrals, investigations, or interventions while also helping clinicians provide appropriate self-care when escalation is not needed.”
The context: Paquet, who is a physiotherapist, told BetaKit in an email that she co-founded Bia in 2016 with other healthcare professionals as a tool to make clinical knowledge more accessible to healthcare professionals by building e-learning modules and a library of medical content. articles.title: Zenzap raises $44M for its AI chat app that aims to replace WhatsApp in the workplace | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Many businesses around the world use consumer-facing chat apps like WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord, or iMessage to talk and coordinate with staff, and exchange documents or data.
Guy Weiss is building Zenzap, a private messenger with AI that wants to help companies communicate with their staff and arm them with their organization’s context while staying in line with IT and security rules.
The company has raised $44 million in funding from investors including Bessemer, Lightspeed, and The Garage, as well as individual investors Wix president Nir Zohar and former GM of EY, Yoram Tietz.
The fundraise is interesting because Weiss is raising money for the first time in his career. In 2012, he bootstrapped e-commerce marketing platform StuccoMedia, and sold it to Market Group in 2015. After that, he became an investor for a few years. In 2022, he founded Zenzap after meeting Bessemer partner Adam Fisher and noodling on different ideas along with his current co-founders Noam Neumann and Jonatan Bien.
Weiss said he initially bootstrapped the app and worked out of Bessemer’s office.
“I didn’t want to raise capital. The only thing I had to lose was my name, and I was super afraid to do a second round as a founder and become a failure, because my first round was very successful. I didn’t need to work for money. So, when I met Adam, I actually started my idea with my own capital,” he told TechCrunch.

articles.title: German robotics unicorn NEURA launches Neuron AI to advance Physical AI and humanoid robotics | EU-Startups
articles.summary:
Metzingen-based NEURA Robotics today introduced Neuron AI, its multimodal foundation model for Physical AI – combining 3D vision, touch, audio, robot state and language with memory – enabling their robots to act on information beyond what the camera sees and even retain context when it disappears from view.
This comes off the back of their previously announced a Series C of up to €1.2 billion in June 2026, following its €120 million Series B in 2025, to support the development and deployment of cognitive robotics, shared intelligence infrastructure and Physical AI systems such as Neuron AI.
“An intelligent robot needs a brain that brings its senses together and remembers what happened,” says David Reger, Founder and CEO of NEURA Robotics. “With Neuron AI, we are building the brain of the physical world: Physical AI that turns human expertise and physical experience into capabilities robots can learn and apply. Developed in Germany, built for the world.”

articles.title: 32GB of DDR5 6000 RAM now costs $450 — AI-induced shortage reaches worst milestone yet
articles.summary:
32GB of DDR5 6000 RAM now costs $450 — AI-induced shortage reaches worst milestone yet
$449.97 to be precise.
The AI-induced PC component shortage, which has caused drastic increases in the cost of DIY building, continues to get worse. Since last year, RAM prices have increased by more than 500% and show no sign of slowing down. In August, we reported that DDR5 6000 RAM — the sweet spot benchmark for both performance and pricing — had reached $400; now, the price is $450.
As mentioned, because DDR5 6000 RAM is a de facto standard configuration and capacity in terms of performance, tracking the price of this particular spec has proven to be a strong barometer of the industry overall. While we track RAM prices across multiple models and kits, we also track the price of 32GB DDR5 6000 RAM daily.
We've been creeping closer to $450 for some time. As of today, the cheapest 32GB DDR5 6000 kit on the market costs $449.97, or three cents shy of $450. Cheaper RAM is still available; this 32GB DDR5 4800 kit is $399 at Corsair, but good, speedy RAM is now harder to buy than ever before. The 4800 Corsair kit once cost just $80.
As RAM prices and other component hikes have a knock-on effect on PC pricing as a whole, it was recently reported that PC shipments in 3Q26 have tumbled by a massive 20%, with the top three vendors shipping 11.6 million fewer units than the same period last year.
Combo deals remain a rare bright spot. Various Newegg bundles could save you as much as $358 when you b…

articles.title: Chrome, Firefox Updates Patch 114 Flaws as Mozilla Unveils Firefox Enterprise
articles.summary:
Google and Mozilla on Tuesday announced fresh Chrome and Firefox updates that resolve 114 vulnerabilities.
The Chrome update was rolled out with fixes for 37 security defects, including seven critical-severity memory issues: a buffer overflow in ANGLE and six use-after-free issues in Browser, PDF, Network, Core, SVG, and Media.
Use-after-free weaknesses represented the majority of the 29 high-severity bugs addressed with the browser refresh. The single medium-severity flaw on the list is also a use-after-free bug.
Per Google’s advisory, at least 15 of the vulnerabilities were reported by Xinyang Ge (Anthropic), assisted by Claude, and no bug bounty reward will be paid for them. Google found 12 security defects.
Google says it handed out $1,000 for a high-severity issue reported by an external researcher, and has yet to disclose the reward amounts for the remaining external reports.
Rolling out as versions 155.0.8059.79/.80 for Windows and macOS, and as version 155.0.8059.79 for Linux, the browser refresh arrived on the same day that Google announced higher bug bounty rewards for some Chrome vulnerabilities.
On Tuesday, Mozilla released Firefox 158 with patches for 77 security defects, most of which were discovered by Mozilla (40) and Amy Burnett of OpenAI (9).
The update resolves 30 high-severity use-after-free, sandbox escape, privilege escalation, information disclosure, incorrect boundary, race condition, JIT miscompilation, and integer overflow bugs.

articles.title: One SoC. Two worlds. Zero compromise: How Red Hat In-Vehicle Operating System and DXC AMBER come together in a mixed-criticality software-defined vehicle solution
articles.summary:
At ELIV 2026 in Baden-Baden, Red Hat and DXC are showcasing a software-defined vehicle (SDV) platform that brings together AD/ADAS and digital cockpit workloads on a single high-performance compute platform, with Red Hat In-Vehicle Operating System providing an ISO 26262 ASIL-B certified Linux foundation for the safety-relevant software domain.
The automotive industry has been exploring ADAS and IVI convergence for years. In collaboration with DXC, we are showcasing a production-grade implementation, running Android Automotive OS, an ASIL-B instrument cluster and AD/ADAS applications side by side on a single Qualcomm Snapdragon Ride Flex SA8775P, part of Qualcomm's Snapdragon Ride Flex family, which is designed to simultaneously support digital cockpit and ADAS workloads.
The key building blocks are Red Hat In-Vehicle Operating System at the heart of the safety-critical software domain and DXC’s AMBER middleware, communication and hardware enablement framework, providing the cross-domain SDV platform integration layer. A Type 1 hypervisor provides isolation between the Android and Red Hat In-Vehicle Operating System software domains, while the SoC’s ASIL-D safety island and an Infineon AURIX companion MCU provide additional safety and vehicle-interface capabilities.

articles.title: Deploy and evaluate models with Amazon SageMaker JumpStart | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Deploy and evaluate models with Amazon SageMaker JumpStart

articles.title: Your database decision could come back to haunt you

Your database decision could come back to haunt you
When building AI prototypes, developers naturally want to get up and running as fast as possible. But move too fast, and those decisions can come back to haunt you if they lead you to make flippant decisions about data infrastructure.
For smaller, less-regulated startups building SaaS or internal applications, the consequences may not be as dire. Wherever you start building, you can usually keep running there even when applications move into production.
But for large-scale enterprises operating in highly regulated environments — think healthcare, finance, government — some developer-friendly database platforms simply can’t meet the security, compliance, deployment, availability, and reliability requirements that emerge when it’s time to shift into production.
Yes, you can re-platform. But it’ll cost you in redevelopment work, labor, and operational overhead. Choosing a database that can support both prototyping and production from Day 1 could let you skip those headaches altogether.
The cost of choosing a database you’ll outgrow
Moving an application from one database platform to another as developers move prototypes into production may not seem like a particularly arduous transaction. Ce vol, qui remonte au 11 juillet, a eu lieu au centre d’essais de Noshiro, dans la préfecture d’Akita, au nord du Japon. Dans la vidéo, on voit la préparation, le vol et ce qui se passe une fois l’engin posé. Pendant la phase de vol, RV-X est monté à environ 11 mètres et s’est décalé de 16 mètres en restant vertical. Le vol a duré une quarantaine de secondes.
Onze mètres de haut, ça peut faire sourire, quand on compare au Starship de SpaceX : l’immense lanceur de l’entreprise américaine en est maintenant à faire des vols orbitaux. Mieux que ça : il devrait bientôt y avoir le premier test de capture de l’étage supérieur par la tour de lancement (le propulseur, lui, a déjà été rattrapé).
Mais c’est oublier que SpaceX aussi a commencé modestement. Le Starhopper, premier engin d’essai du programme Starship, ressemblait beaucoup à ce RV-X : un prototype extrêmement incomplet. Lors de son premier vol libre, en juillet 2019, il ne s’était élevé que d’une vingtaine de mètres.
Le Japon n’est pas le seul à courir derrière SpaceX. La veille du vol de RV-X, les médias d’État chinois annonçaient que la Chine avait récupéré po…

articles.title: The unfinished business of a startup's collapse
articles.summary:
First published on October 11, 2026
Image Source: TechCabal
Koko Networks raised more than $100 million from international investors to sell subsidised clean cooking stoves, relying on carbon credit sales to help cover their costs. Copia Global raised $123 million to bring e-commerce to smaller towns. Both businesses built sizeable operations around costly problems in African markets. When they collapsed, the question became how much money was left to repay those who had financed their growth.
In February 2026, the administrators of Copia estimated the realisable value of its assets at KES 206.6 million ($1.6 million), while its liabilities were considerably greater than that figure. Similarly, Koko Networks (UK) Limited had accumulated significant debt as a result of regulatory and commercial problems that had disrupted its carbon credit business.
The two failures expose a less visible side of venture capital. Raising millions and reaching customers does not guarantee that a business will have enough cash or saleable assets to meet its obligations. When the money runs out, investors are not the only ones who lose. Suppliers, employees and lenders must pursue claims against what remains, often through lengthy court proceedings that determine who gets paid and how much.

articles.title: US Arrests Two in Crackdown on North Korean IT Worker Laptop Farms
articles.summary:
Two US nationals were arrested in a new law enforcement operation targeting fraudulent North Korean IT worker schemes.
The suspects, Michael James Bostelle of Pennsylvania and Juan Cecilio Pena Carrillo of Texas, allegedly helped North Korean IT workers (ITWs) illegally obtain remote work at US companies.
According to a four-count indictment, the multi-year fraud scheme by Bostelle, Pena, and their co-conspirators generated over $3 million in fraudulent revenue.
As part of the scheme, which allegedly ran between 2019 and July 2025, the two housed and configured laptops issued by victim US companies so ITWs would appear to work from the US.
Using fake IDs and VPN and proxy infrastructure masking their real locations, the ITWs, aided by US facilitators, obtained employment at over 70 US companies in the communications, cyber support, healthcare, manufacturing, and retail sectors.
The indictment also charges China-based Sun Sheng Ming, Pei Li Guang, Weng Shou Cheng, Han Guo Bin, Wang Jian Jun, Sheng Zhang Kun, Zhang Wei Ping, Zhang Li Ping, Yu Yang, and Jin Long for participating in the scheme.
In a separate effort named Operation Lonestar Roundup, the FBI searched 40 locations in Texas suspected of operating as laptop farms for ITWs and seized 187 laptops and KVM devices used to commit fraud.

Where do you look when Kubernetes is healthy but requests stall?
In cloud-native operations, few scenarios are as maddening as the “phantom slowdown.” This happens when Grafana or Kubernetes dashboards show a sea of green: pods are running, liveness and readiness probes return success codes, and node CPU utilization stays well below capacity limits. Yet users submit urgent tickets complaining of sporadic, severe latency when querying an application or waiting for an AI model’s response.
Why do basic health checks pass inspection while application performance degrades? And how can engineering teams trace the root cause when the issue is intermittent and spans multi-tier hybrid infrastructure?
To understand the mechanics of these sometimes evasive performance regressions, The New Stack spoke with Mahesh Ramachandran, who leads product management for HPE OpsRamp Software.
Ramachandran tells TNS how continuous telemetry and retrospective analysis help teams investigate intermittent slowdowns, and how AI-assisted investigation can complement dashboards.

articles.title: Todas las empresas de IA quieren crear sus propios chips, así que Nvidia quiere ahora tener su propia IA

Nvidia se ha convertido en el pegamento de la IA por su tecnología, pero también por sus inversiones. El gigante estadounidense ha logrado que sus chips sean los más deseados en la fase de entrenamiento de la inteligencia artificial, pero ahora que esas mismas empresas a las que alimentaba están buscando la forma de darle la espalda, parece que han tomado la decisión de pagar con la misma moneda.
¿Cómo? Teniendo su propia IA que además sea la punta de lanza de los modelos abiertos como respuesta a la estrategia china. Y Reflection AI sería la joya que falta en el guantelete de Nvidia.
En corto. En un artículo del Financial Times en el que cita fuentes con información directa, se expone que Nvidia está negociando para adquirir Reflection AI o, al menos, profundizar en su relación con ella. Según el medio, las conversaciones están en una fase temprana y, aunque el trato podría formalizarse a lo largo de las próximas semanas, ninguna de las partes ha querido declarar nada.
Vías. Sobre la mesa hay varias fórmulas, siendo la más drástica una por la que Nvidia, directamente, realiza la compra completa de la empresa. Sin embargo, hay otras vías:
- Más capital - Nvidia ya es uno de los mayores accionistas de Reflection y la vía fácil sería invertir aún más.

articles.title: Une supernova presque en direct : le télescope James Webb a vu une étoile quelques jours après son explosion - Numerama
articles.summary:
Vues depuis la Terre, les supernovae peuvent ressembler à des étoiles ordinaires. Pourtant, il s’agit de l’explosion extrêmement puissante d’une étoile en fin de vie. Pour les plus massives, le cœur s’effondre sur lui-même avant que l’astre ne vole en éclats.
Généralement, la lumière émise lors de l’explosion reste visible quelques semaines, voire quelques mois pour les plus massives, et il faut être réactif pour pouvoir capter le maximum de données avant que le tout devienne invisible.
Dans une étude pas encore relue par des pairs, parue le 29 septembre sur le serveur arXiv et repérée par le site Phys.org, une équipe menée par l’astronome Ming-Yang Zhuang, de l’Université de l’Illinois à Urbana-Champaign, fait état d’une probable supernova détectée seulement quatre à dix jours après l’explosion. Le signal se nomme AT 2026abck et se trouve extrêmement loin dans l’Univers, à un redshift (le décalage de sa lumière vers le rouge, qui trahit son éloignement) de 5,017, ce qui signifie que lorsque la lumière a été émise, l’Univers était âgé d’un peu plus d’un milliard d’années.
Le télescope James Webb passe et repasse
Ce type de trouvaille aussi loin dans le temps est assez rare. On compte seulement 200 supernovae découvertes à des distances équivalentes autour d’un redshift de 4. Les phénomènes de lentilles gravitationnelles, qui font un effet loupe, sont particulièrement pratiques pour pouvoir repérer ces sources très lumineuses mais aussi extrêmement lointaines et donc difficile…

articles.title: The US military’s race to make fake blood

The US military’s race to make fake blood
DARPA is funding a redoubled effort to develop a shelf-stable substitute for what field medics and trauma doctors need most: more blood.
Its call sign was Morphine 1-2.
In February 2007, the hulking dual-rotor casualty evacuation helicopter had just flown three wounded soldiers to a field hospital in Balad, north of Baghdad, when another call came: an emergency mission to fly through an insurgent-controlled area in broad daylight. Typically, helicopters would be in a spot like this only at night, and with all lights turned off.
As it passed near the city of Karmah, in the eastern side of Al-Anbar province, an insurgent fired a portable missile launcher. The tail gunner, who likely saw the shot roaring in, yelled for the pilot to make an evasive move. But the missile had already locked on, and the ensuing blast started a fire on board. After the pilot battled the failing machine for 58 agonizing seconds, Morphine 1-2 plunged to the ground. All seven crew members were killed.
Why was the helo there in daylight? “It was getting blood and bringing it back. It was [on] what we call a ‘blood run,’ and [it’s] the highest of priorities besides casualty evacuation,” explains Lieutenant Commander Robert Murray, a Navy officer and program manager at DARPA, the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, who studied this incident as an intelligence officer.

It depends on the circumstances, and as we'll explain, things can get a little complicated.
Understanding Driver Overhead and CPU Bottlenecks

L'histoire sur laquelle OpenAI a dû s'exprimer mardi 13 octobre a des airs de roman d'espionnage, mais version Silicon Valley. Un ingénieur d'OpenAI, de nationalité saoudienne, a en effet été arrêté pour avoir, selon la justice américaine, dissimulé pendant plusieurs jours un enregistreur audio branché sur un port USB dans une salle de réunion fréquentée par la direction de la firme qui propulse ChatGPT, à San Francisco. L'appareil, emmailloté dans du papier toilette et branché derrière une télévision, a été découvert fin septembre par des salariés. Selon la plainte des procureurs fédéraux, le dossier contre cet ingénieur, depuis licencié, repose notamment sur des images de vidéosurveillance, un second enregistreur retrouvé dans un sac contenant ses papiers et des requêtes adressées à un robot conversationnel.

Dans la grande famille des enceintes connectées, les HomePod d’Apple ont globalement bonne réputation. Il y a cependant un point que la marque semble ignorer depuis longtemps : les touches fantômes. Autrement dit, des activations involontaires de l’écran tactile situé au sommet des enceintes. La 4e bêta d’iOS 27.2, publiée ce mardi 13 octobre, montre qu’Apple prépare enfin un correctif.
On trouve de nombreux témoignages de ce souci, que ce soit sur les réseaux sociaux comme Reddit ou sur les forums officiels d’Apple. Les utilisateurs se plaignent du volume qui change de niveau, de la lecture qui s’arrête ou passe au média suivant, voire de Siri qui s’active. Le tout sans qu’ils soient à l’origine de la commande.
Le phénomène est tel qu’il a motivé une entreprise de réparation américaine à proposer le remplacement de l’écran tactile des HomePod, jugé défectueux, par un modèle non officiel.
Les autres solutions évoquées sont plus ou moins extrêmes, de la modification de quelques réglages dans l’application Maison jusqu’à l’ouverture de l’enceinte pour débrancher la dalle tactile.
Côté réglages, deux options limitent les dégâts. Dans l’application Maison, les réglages d’accessibilité du HomePod proposent une adaptation du toucher : en activant la durée de maintien, réglable jusqu’à quatre secondes, l’enceinte ignore les contacts trop brefs. On peut aussi couper l’activation de Siri par appui prolongé. Ces réglages contournent le problème sans réparer la dalle.

articles.title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates may trigger Remote Desktop failures
articles.summary:
Microsoft has confirmed that non-admin users may be unable to connect to devices via Remote Desktop after installing recent Windows updates if the "Administrator protection" security feature is enabled.
This feature began rolling out with the KB5067036 preview cumulative update to systems running Windows 11 24H2/25H2 in October 2025, and it is now enabled by default in organizations using Windows security baselines after installing the October 2026 Windows security update.
When toggled on, admin protection ensures logged-in users have only standard user permissions and prompts them to authenticate via Windows Hello (PIN or biometric) when they try to install new apps or change the Windows registry.
On Tuesday, Microsoft confirmed that Remote Desktop connections may fail with error 0xC000000D after installing the KB5124010 September 2026 non-security preview update or later updates on systems running Windows 11 24H2/25H2/26H1/26H2.
"Attempts to connect might fail with error 0xC000000D and display the message, 'The token that was passed to the function is invalid.' This issue primarily affects enterprise-managed remote devices used as Remote Desktop hosts with Administrator protection enabled, regardless of how the feature was enabled," it said.

articles.title: The task trap: Why AI's biggest promise has nothing to do with speed
articles.summary:
The task trap: Why AI's biggest promise has nothing to do with speed
Business value requires strategic domain expertise rather than task speed
Every week, another headline celebrates how AI made some task faster. A developer wrote code 55% faster. A marketer generated a first-draft blog post in minutes. A product manager summarized a 200-page requirements document in seconds. These are real numbers.
But they are the wrong numbers to celebrate.
Chief Growth Officer at Siemens Digital Industries Software.
If you step back and ask the harder question — what actually creates enterprise value? — task speed is rarely the bottleneck. Where the value traffic gets jammed is almost always upstream, in the question that precedes the task:
It’s not “What do we want IT to build?”
It’s “Why do we want IT to build it?”
It’s not “Why do we need that blog post?”
It’s “What content will drive business impact?”

It’s not “Which process should be optimized?”
It should be “How do we address the quality escape generating rework and scrap?” or “How do we prevent supply chain delays compounding into missed delivery commitments?”
These are questions that AI still cannot answer for you. And the gap between task automation and outcome generation is the defining challenge of this agentic era.

Meet Prismm, a startup that helps banks keep families’ money in-house after an account holder dies. It does this by building beneficiary and estate planning into accounts from day one, which makes the transfer of assets to heirs less complicated. Prismm is presenting its mission today on the Startup Battlefield stage at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.
Prismm was founded in 2020 by sisters Martha Underwood and Shella Sylla, who each have decades of experience in banking and finance. The pair came up with the idea for Prismm based on their own experience of seeing firsthand how difficult it can be to manage a family’s affairs in an emergency.
Their father was hospitalized in 2017 after he fell while helping clear a tree from a neighbor’s roof following Hurricane Irma in Miami. Their mother, who had always relied on him to handle the family’s finances and paperwork, didn’t know where all the important documents and financial information were, and neither did they. Their father recovered, but the experience of not knowing how to access critical information stuck with them.
That was the starting point for Prismm, but the idea really took shape three years later, when Underwood was working at a bank during the COVID-19 pandemic. She saw families come in after a loved one had died, scrambling to find accounts, understand bills, and figure out how to support the surviving spouse.

articles.title: Scientists create super ice that's almost as tough as concrete
articles.summary:
TL;DR: Anyone who's fallen face-first on thick ice will testify that it's pretty strong. But it's nothing compared to a new type of ice created by researchers. The aptly nicknamed super ice is an incredible 10 times stronger under compression than regular frozen water, making it close to the strength of concrete.
Called BioPykrete, the material was developed by a team led by researchers at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. It combines ice, tiny plant-derived cellulose crystals, and a specially engineered protein. The resulting composite also absorbs around 70 times more energy before breaking than ordinary ice.
Regular ice can fail suddenly as cracks race through it. But BioPykrete deforms and gives way more gradually, potentially making it a more useful building material. So not only can it withstand pressure, it can also avoid shattering without warning.
"We wanted to go beyond simply mixing fibers into ice and instead control how the different materials connect at the molecular level," said Professor Ido Braslavsky, one of the lead researchers.
The cellulose nanocrystals form a three-dimensional network around microscopic pockets of ice during freezing. The protein, called CBM3a-AFPIII, connects the ingredients in a glue-like fashion. One part attaches to ice, while the other binds to cellulose.
The researchers believe that this reinforced network helps stop cracks from spreading freely. Adding the protein doubled both compressive strength and energy absorption compared …

articles.title: Apple researchers turn idle Macs into a virtual GPU cloud with ‘Minions’ — researchers say the distributed scheme could scale globally and support model training
articles.summary:
Apple researchers turn idle Macs into a virtual GPU cloud with ‘Minions’ — researchers say the distributed scheme could scale globally and support model training
Can start with a simple request over Slack, but teams worry about their data running on devices outside their group.
Apple internally uses a system known as “Minions,” a “virtual GPU cloud” made up of idle Macs, to help manage workloads, as described in a recent arXiv paper published by its researchers. The system helps take stalled AI jobs, some that once had 10-plus-hour company GPU queues, and distributes them to Macs on the network, with resulting wait times down to as little as minutes. A request from a user on the company’s Slack can get the ball rolling, although the researchers observed a common concern about teams’ data running on devices outside their group.
The paper, also shared on Apple’s Machine Learning Research site, describes the system as having a “Minion Server,” a “Minion Executor,” and a “Minion Watchdog.” The system relies specifically on Apple Silicon for AI inference, the only type of work it does. There are two kinds of jobs: embeddings with open-source Hugging Face transformer models, and text generation from large language models through Ollama, which is installed on each participating Mac.
The Minion Server works by splitting submitted tasks into subtasks, stored in a PostgreSQL database. Then, on each Mac, a Minion Executor is run to pull the next subtask over REST APIs; there is no centr…

articles.title: The Download: faking blood and the future of batteries
articles.summary:
The Download: faking blood and the future of batteries
Plus: The FBI has arrested an OpenAI engineer accused of snooping.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
The US military’s race to make fake blood
In February 2007, a US military helicopter carrying blood to a field hospital was shot down in Iraq, killing all seven crew members. The mission was a reminder of the risks of transporting blood, which has a limited shelf life and is often in short supply.
Now, a $73 million DARPA effort aims to create shelf-stable versions of plasma, platelets, and red blood cells. The idea is to develop dried blood products that can be stored for long periods and deployed quickly on the battlefield.
The project aims to have bags of dried blood products deployed in the field by 2029. But getting it all done will be tough, and researchers still have major questions about the safety and effectiveness of synthetic alternatives.

articles.title: What investors really want to know about IP | EU-Startups
articles.summary:
European startups raised €21.45 billion ($24 billion) in the second quarter of this year, the region’s strongest quarter for venture funding in four years, according to Crunchbase. On the surface, capital is back.
Look one level down and the picture changes. 65% of that money went to 42 companies raising rounds of €90 million ($100 million) or more. Investors are also becoming more disciplined about where that capital goes. OMERS Ventures described its outlook for 2026 as a “return to discipline,” with deeper diligence around traction, retention, defensibility and resilience.
The bar for raising has gone up, but not for the reason most founders assume. It was never that investors stopped writing cheques. It is that they are choosing harder, and one of the places that scrutiny shows up is the moment they ask a founder about intellectual property.
Investors are not asking whether you have patents
When an investor asks about IP, they rarely mean it in the literal sense. “We’ve filed three applications” tells them almost nothing. They want to know whether the founder understands which part of the company is genuinely hard to copy, and whether the protection in place covers it.
Two things are happening here, though most founders only see one of them.

articles.title: SA's KhayaHR builds AI-first workforce platform for frontline economy - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
South African startup KhayaHR is building an AI-first workforce platform for the country’s frontline economy, and has already signed up more than 12,000 workers since launching in May.
Founded by Jacques Roux, KhayaHR gives workers a portable digital workforce passport. Employers can use it to find, assess, hire and then manage frontline staff in one place.
“Most recruitment technology assumes that candidates already have formal CVs, established digital histories and easily verifiable employment records,” Roux told Disrupt Africa.
“That assumption excludes many frontline workers. Their work experience may be informal, references fragmented, certificates stored as photographs or paper documents, and availability known only through personal networks or WhatsApp groups.”
The worker passport holds identity and right-to-work confirmation, skills, experience, references, employer recommendations, certificates, availability, and optional voice or video introductions. Workers cannot publish a profile until their identity and right to work in South Africa have been confirmed.
On the employer side, Khaya AI turns a natural-language hiring requirement into a structured search of the available workforce.
“An employer can describe the role, location and experience they need, and Khaya AI converts that into a structured search,” said Roux. “Employers can then assess real profile evidence, connect with suitable workers and manage employment through KhayaHR’s HR and payroll system.”
