Generative-AI workloads evolve on a quarterly cadence, with novel attention variants, quantization formats, and routing schemes appearing faster than fixed-function neural-processor silicon can be respun. AI sector wipeout risks global financial contagion, IMF report warns — 14 deals drove $1.4 trillion in circular orders on $650B in loans
Report explores how AI financing could harm the global economy if the industry fails to deliver
Watchers and reporters in the AI space have long pointed out how its circular economy could implode, potentially taking associated investments with it. The IMF has examined those fears in its latest Global Financial Stability Report, and its conclusions are stark. In the IMF's view, the global economy is becoming increasingly dependent on capital flows to the AI world, and a crash could result in harm to global GDP, investment, and consumption by 2028.
The report makes a distinction between "core" AI firms and others in the space. Presumably, core firms include companies like TSMC, Nvidia, and AMD, memory makers like SK hynix and Micron, and storage vendors like Western Digital. Those firms are seeing historical windfalls, and most of their production is currently spoken for years in advance. In other words, in this gold rush, these are the companies making bank selling the shovels.
In theory, if non-core players fail, only their investors would suffer harm, but according to the report, there's still risk to worry about. articles.title: The AI race is back on
articles.summary:
Last week, Anthropic and OpenAI looked like they had the AI race to themselves, pulling ahead with increasingly powerful models that left their rivals in the dust. Google seemed hopelessly far behind, while Meta, despite spending billions to revive its floundering AI ambitions, had yet to establish itself as a serious contender. Even the latest models coming out of China, impressive as they were, appeared to be playing catch-up.
The AI race is back on
Google and Meta are challenging Anthropic and OpenAI at the AI frontier.
Then, in the space of a few days, everything changed. Google and Meta both unveiled frontier models they claim can go toe to toe with the best from OpenAI and Anthropic. Suddenly, the race is back on — and it’s anyone’s game.
Until this week, Google looked like it had permanently lost its place among the AI front-runners. Since releasing Gemini 3 late last year, the tech giant had delivered little more than incremental improvements. Gemini 3 was formidable when it launched, but its lead was fleeting, and it struggled to keep up with later offerings from OpenAI and Anthropic, or even some of the open-weight models emerging from China.
A series of internal shake-ups only added to the sense that Google was retreating from the AI frontier. Veteran executive Jeff Dean departed the company with a number of other AI researchers to launch a new startup. articles.title: Mosqitter is turning its mosquito traps into an AI-powered surveillance network | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Mosquitoes and the diseases they carry are expanding into new territory. Rising temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, and global travel are reshaping where disease-carrying mosquitoes can thrive, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Cases of dengue, a viral illness spread by mosquito bites, more than doubled in a year, from 6.5 million reported globally in 2023 to a record 14.6 million in 2024, the WHO says.
A 30-person, Pennsylvania-based startup, Mosqitter, thinks fighting that problem requires more than killing mosquitoes. The company started by building chemical-free devices that lure and trap female mosquitoes by mimicking the heat, scent, and breathing cues of humans.
Anastasiia Romanova, co-founder and CEO of Mosqitter, told TechCrunch that the company set out to bring more sustainable mosquito-control products to a market still heavily reliant on chemicals. Romanova says it now has more than 5,000 devices operating across five continents, up from just over 250 when TechCrunch last covered the company in 2022. The startup now wants to turn its traps into an AI-powered monitoring network that can identify mosquito species, track changes in their numbers, and give earlier warnings about emerging disease risks.

articles.title: Google Antigravity SDK Adds Local Model Support for Greater Token Efficiency and Code Privacy
articles.summary:
Google has introduced support for local models in the Antigravity SDK, enabling developers to build and execute agentic workflows directly on their own machines, while retaining the flexibility to mix in cloud-based models for higher-level tasks. This approach gives developers greater control over data privacy, inference costs, network dependencies, and computational workload distribution.
One of the most compelling capabilities of the Antigravity SDK is hybrid agent orchestration, which adapts Google's proposed Architect-Builder pattern to a mixed cloud-local compute environment.
According to the Architect-Builder pattern, one primary, high-context AI agent, the architect, holds the macro-level system view, including dependencies, architectural guardrails, and detailed specifications or implementation plans. Once the architect has defined a plan, several parallel, multiple specialized AI agents, the builders, work independently in isolated environments to execute discrete, narrow tasks mapped out by the specification.
Google says that the Antigravity SDK enables the architect to operate in the cloud, devising a strategy and breaking the task into smaller units using filenames and task descriptions, without requiring access to the source code itself. The builders, instead, run locally and perform tasks such as reproducing security vulnerabilities, proposing code fixes, reviewing candidate patches, and running regression tests. In a particularly ironic twist, prosecutors allege that a chatbot helped with the scheme. An account associated with Alfozan's spouse submitted questions about continuous recording, Wi-Fi connectivity, live listening, and encryption. Some prompts even referenced the device's unique MAC address.
Alfozan also allegedly used a productivity tool to locate executives and research meeting rooms and calendars. The targeted room hosted discussions about proprietary research, products, government engagements, and other sensitive matters.

It’s dubbed the Cross-Sector Anti-Fraud Exchange (CSAFE) and it comes in partnership between Bell, Rogers and Telus’ digital security joint venture EnStream and BMO, CIBC, Desjardins, National Bank, Scotiabank and RBC.
Together, the companies aim to improve data protection for Canadians by sharing confirmed fraud intelligence between participating institutions using EnStream. Agentic AI changes the CPU performance problem. Key Takeaways
- A commerce platform tends to age better when it is built from a small number of first-class entities that reference each other rather than duplicate data between them. - When a feature has to satisfy several independent constraints at once — which locations can serve a customer, which offerings are enabled where, which categories carry extra eligibility rules — treating the problem as an intersection of independently-evaluated sets scales better than threading conditional logic through a single workflow.
- Grouping related items under a shared identity, with its own completeness guarantees, keeps a bundled offering from silently degrading into something that no longer matches what was promised to the customer.
- Regulated or constrained product categories are easier to support safely when their constraints are modeled as a distinct type carrying its own rules, rather than as flags scattered through a shared code path. New categories then become additive, rather than compounding the complexity of existing ones.
- When a fully safe editing workflow is not realistic within a launch deadline, a layered set of lighter-weight guards can capture most of the risk reduction at a fraction of the engineering cost — often enough of a trade-off to ship safely under real time pressure.

articles.title: Dunkle Energie: So könnten schwache Radiowellen sein Geheimnis lüften
articles.summary:
Dunkle Energie: Ein schwaches Radiosignal aus der Frühzeit des Universums könnte ihr Geheimnis lüften
Was steckt hinter Dunkler Energie? Dies ist eines der großen Rätsel der Kosmologie. Die unsichtbare, hypothetische Form der Energie gilt als verantwortlich für die Ausdehnung des Universums, nachdem der erste Schub durch den Big Bang abgeklungen war.
Neuer Weg zum Verständnis von Dunkler Energie?
Direkt nachgewiesen werden konnte die Dunkle Energie, die fast 70 Prozent der Energiedichte des Universums ausmachen soll, noch nicht. Ein Forschungsteam könnte aber nun einen Weg gefunden haben, Dunkle Energie künftig besser zu verstehen.
Die Resultate ihrer Forschung haben die Wissenschaftler:innen in gleich zwei Papern vorgestellt, die beide in der Fachzeitschrift The Astrophysical Journal erschienen sind.
Analyse von neutralem Wasserstoff
Die Forschenden haben mit dem Radioteleskop Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) nach Spuren von kosmischem Wasserstoff gesucht. Genauer gesagt nach neutralem atomaren Wasserstoff, der nicht ionisiert und also elektrisch ungeladen ist.

The fintech’s figure offers a glimpse into the economics of digital credit in Nigeria’s consumer lending market, estimated to be worth $2.1 billion. Lenders must price loans to cover defaults, funding and operating costs, with borrowers who repay on time potentially bearing part of the cost of lending to those who do not.

"This exploit chain combined an authentication bypass, a remote code execution (RCE), and a privilege escalation vulnerability to achieve unauthenticated root-level code execution. The RCE and authentication bypass vulnerabilities are tracked under CVE-2026-104935," Volexity said.

articles.title: Characterization of HBM Power Consumption (ETH Zurich, NYU)
articles.summary:
Researchers at ETH Zürich and New York University published a technical paper titled “Understanding the Power Consumption of Modern High Bandwidth Memory: Experimental Analysis and Modeling Using Real HBM2 DRAM Chips.”
Abstract Excerpt:
“We perform the first comprehensive experimental characterization of power consumed by real HBM2 DRAM chips. Our extensive characterization yields 1) the empirical basis for developing new, accurate HBM power models or validating existing power models and 2) key insights into structural and data-pattern-dependent variation of power in HBM2 chips. Out of our 13 new findings and 6 key takeaway messages, we highlight: 1) a read operation consumes significantly higher current than any other operation and 2) the toggled data bus signals in a data transfer burst significantly affect current draw where toggling all HBM2-internal bank group bus signals causes 29.4% higher power consumption than keeping them constant. Leveraging our empirical insights into HBM2 power consumption, we engineer an access pattern that yields 23.6% higher power consumption on average across 36 tested HBM2 chips than the highest-power-consuming JEDEC-specified current measurement loop.”

Hillel Wayne: I have a bit of a weird job. Companies pay me to find bugs in systems that don't exist, or more specifically, don't yet exist. It's actually a relatively simple process that all of us can do. To show you that this is just even possible in the first place, let's walk through the thing doer.

It also quickly follows Donald Trump’s September 29, 2026 Executive Order to “replace the term ‘Artificial Intelligence’ (‘AI’) with ‘Super Intelligence’ (‘SI’) in the executive branch.”
The problem, however, is that ‘superintelligence’ (one word) has long been used for a specific quality of AI. It was defined by Oxford philosopher Nick Bostrom in 2014 as, ‘Any intellect that greatly exceeds the cognitive performance of humans in virtually all domains of interest.’ It is consequently more akin or superior to artificial general intelligence (AGI), which is in turn superior to common or garden AI.
So, is Booz Allen referring to frontier AI in line with Trump’s executive order, or something more advanced in line with Bostrom’s ‘superintelligence’? articles.title: How Y-Queue Prepared Emmanuel Obiechina for Fintech

Building Y-Queue took Emmanuel Obiechina and his co-founders just three weeks. Convincing people to use it proved to be an entirely different education.
Long before he conceived Kira AI—his WhatsApp-based banking and payments platform—Obiechina saw a clean engineering solution to a persistent campus headache. At the University of Nigeria, Nsukka (UNN), students routinely struggled to order meals from restaurants scattered across the university town in Enugu State. Y-Queue was designed as his parting gift to the student body: an on-demand bridge between hungry undergraduates and local kitchens, built with the ambition of eventually capturing the wider food delivery market across Enugu city.
On a screen, the product was seamless. On the ground, the stubborn friction of physical logistics quickly took over. Clean code could route a ticket in milliseconds, but it could not force overwhelmed kitchen staff to prep meals faster, guarantee dispatch riders arrived on time, or persuade cash-conscious students that convenience was worth an extra delivery fee.
Obiechina had entered the venture with years of programming experience and a track record of shipping software for international engineering teams. Yet Y-Queue confronted him with a brand of operational chaos that no algorithm could optimise away.
“Programming is actually the easy part,” Obiechina reflects. “The difficult part of building a company is what happens after you have built it.”

Novidade acelera regulamentação anti-spam prevista pela Anatel e prevê autenticação de chamadas por parte das operadoras.

Data center boom across Europe could well lead to higher electricity prices, report warns
Europe could be next to face data center-related price hikes

- Government intervention is likely needed to protect billpayers
New Moody's data has warned that Europe's growing data center footprint could severely impact energy prices across the continent as we're already seeing in the US.
As of 2025, Europe's data center-related electricity consumption stood at around 2.5% of the entire continent's consumption, however within the space of a decade (by 2035), this could more than double to 5.7% across countries like France and the UK.
But more worryingly, the countries that are set to play host to the most capacity will likely see even starker rises, including the Northlands (17%) and Ireland (30%).
European data centers could push energy prices up
Moody's explained that, while data centers would typically pay for any upgrades needed for their direct connection, the grid operator usually picks up the bill for wider network reinforcement. Those additional costs, as well as a tighter supply-demand imbalances, could push costs onto the end user – you and I.

articles.summary:
If you’re a watch enthusiast, you probably don’t want to exchange your prized timepiece for a bulky fitness tracker. But Hiyd founder Salah Batroukh doesn’t think people should have to sacrifice fashion for function.
“We don’t think that health tracking needs to be this overly conscious decision where you have to change something about the way you look,” Batroukh told TechCrunch. “That’s the ethos of the entire company. Our plan is to build out this product ecosystem of invisible health tracking.”
Hiyd’s first device to make health tracking look cooler is a small, slim disc that attaches to the back of your watch via microsuction, a material technology that allows the sensor to sit flush under your watch without magnets or adhesive. That way, it won’t leave any residue or mess with the mechanics of watches that keep time using magnets.
“Microsuction is essentially a textured silicone, with hundreds of tiny pockets per square inch molded into a pliable sheet. So when you press on it, it pushes air out of all those pockets, and you end up with a vacuum — just like traditional suction cups but scaled down incredibly,” Batroukh explained. “It works incredibly at stopping shear forces, but a little bit of prying allows it to pop right off, which is ideal for us. It’s also incredibly thin at just 0.3 mm with our manufacturing processes.”

articles.title: Meta Extends Confidential Computing to AI Glasses with Private Processing
articles.summary:
Meta has extended Private Processing to AI glasses, using confidential virtual machines (CVMs) for sensitive AI workloads and persistent user context in the cloud. The design combines Trusted Execution Environment (TEEs), remote attestation, anonymous credentials, OHTTP, and encrypted storage. Meta says it supports streaming transcription, contextual search, and long-term recall requiring more computing and persistent state.
Basic interactions, such as calls and messages, can run on the glasses, while more advanced workloads require larger models and access to personal context accumulated over time. Meta introduced Private Processing for WhatsApp and Meta AI in 2025 and is now extending the architecture to wearable AI workloads.
Oskar Linde, VP of XR Technologies at Meta, described the approach on LinkedIn as a way to make AI more useful throughout the day while supporting the stateful, personal context required by AI glasses without allowing Meta to access that data.
The architecture moves the confidential computing boundary from the device into Meta's cloud infrastructure. AI models run inside confidential virtual machines (CVMs) backed by hardware TEEs, with processor encrypted memory. Meta says the boundary spans CPUs and GPUs, allowing mixed workloads to remain protected.

articles.title: NIMC: Nigeria’s national identity database is hosted locally

Nigeria’s National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) says its national identity database is hosted entirely in Nigeria and managed by its own employees, as digital identity verification becomes increasingly important to public services.
Alvan Ikoku, director of NIMC’s Strategic Programme Office, disclosed this during a briefing with journalists on Wednesday, addressing concerns about where Nigerians’ identity data is stored, who controls the infrastructure, and how the commission protects it from leaks.
“It is being managed by Nigerians, not Nigerian vendors, by NIMC employees,” Ikoku said. He maintained that NIMC has never hosted its identity data outside the country, does not use cloud hosting for its core database, and has disaster recovery systems to keep services running when systems fail.

Local hosting alone cannot guarantee security; tight access controls, monitoring, and accountability for misuse are also critical.

O primeiro permite jogar títulos de PS2 no console, enquanto o segundo é focado em burlar o sistema para instalar apps e jogos indisponíveis na PS Store. articles.title: Simulations Pinpoint Leakage Pathway In GAAFETs (Sandia, Luxembourg)
articles.summary:
Researchers at Sandia National Laboratories and Luxembourg Institute of Science and Technology published a technical paper titled “Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations.”
Abstract Excerpt:
“Gate-All-Around Field-Effect Transistors (GAAFETs) are emerging as successors to Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) and are central to continued scaling at advanced semiconductor nodes. Despite their improved electrostatic control, recent measurements show that the drain current in GAAFETs deviates strongly from thermionic behavior at negative gate voltages, increasing as the gate voltage becomes more negative. This leakage has been attributed to direct gate-drain tunneling through the high-k dielectric, enhanced by drain-induced dielectric barrier lowering (DIDBL). Here, we use predictive, charge-self-consistent Non-Equilibrium Green Function (NEGF) simulations based on the Contact Block Reduction (CBR) method to spatially resolve this leakage pathway in GAAFETs.”
Find the technical paper here. October 2026.
Mamaluy, Denis, Juan P. Mendez, Coleman Cariker, Michael Titze, and Alex A. Belianinov. “Revealing New Leakage Paths in GAAFETs using Predictive First-Principles Simulations.” arXiv preprint arXiv:2610.14298 (October 2026). https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2610.14298. Creative Commons license.

articles.summary:
In brief: There are a few ways to play PC games on Android devices such as phones, but it often requires streaming them, which isn't always ideal, and may require a subscription. But a free, open-source app brings Valve's Steam client to supported Snapdragon-powered Android devices, running games locally and without changing the OS.
Called DroidDeck, the app runs PC games locally using ARM64 Proton and x86 translation. There's no streaming, and it doesn't ask for root access or to replace Android with a different operating system.
DroidDeck runs Valve's ARM64 Linux Steam client in Big Picture mode, so it should be pretty familiar. Windows games run through Proton, while FEX handles x86 instruction translation.
Steam users can access their libraries directly and download the games onto the device, just like they would on a PC.
The app also boasts GPU driver switching, AMD FSR and Snapdragon GSR upscaling, and frame generation through Lossless Scaling, provided you own a copy on Steam.
DroidDeck won't work on every Android device out there. According to the project's GitHub page, you'll need Android 9 or newer and supported Adreno graphics, officially Adreno 730 or newer, including the 8xx series. Adreno 6xx support is experimental, while Mali, Xclipse, PowerVR and Adreno 710 aren't supported.
You'll also need around 3GB for the Linux runtime, another 1.1GB if you want the optional desktop and emulators, and plenty of space for your games.

articles.title: Netflix lays off 1,000 people in biggest layoffs in years
articles.summary:
Netflix has axed six per cent of its workforce, or roughly 1,000 employees.
Via Variety, the streamer confirmed the layoffs in an internal memo. Per the memo, most of the cuts are in the company’s product, technology, legal and HR teams. This is Netflix’s biggest round of layoffs since it let go of around 450 people in 2022.
Co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters say “decisions like these are never easy” but that its mission to “entertain the world […] requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources.” The executives add that they’ll “continue to invest aggressively in high impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation.”
This comes after Sarandos admitted just two weeks ago that Netflix is “not growing as fast as I want us to.” Part of Netflix’s efforts to drive growth have been to diversify its content slate with the likes of live programming, including NFL games and the exclusive reveal of Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay. That said, Netflix’s other gaming-related efforts haven’t paid off, with the streamer shuttering multiple studios over the past few years, including, most prominently, Night School Studio, mere weeks after it released its latest title, the interactive thriller Unhinged.
Netflix is set to report Q3 earnings next week, so more information on its content plans should come then.

El formato físico en el aire, la PS5 completamente abierta a modificaciones y una versión de PC como horizonte lejano. O no, porque varias voces del sector sostienen que la espera será mucho más corta. En concreto, de unos tres o cuatro meses.
Las fuentes apuntan a 2027. El medio especializado GamesBeat ha hablado con cuatro personas que, supuestamente, conocen los planes de Rockstar. De las conversaciones ha salido una ventana de lanzamiento para el 'GTA VI' de PC: el primer trimestre de 2027. Llegaría poco después del estreno en consolas, que se fijó para el 19 de noviembre de 2026.
Según ha explicado el medio:
"GamesBeat ha podido confirmar, a través de cuatro fuentes de la industria conocedoras de los planes del estudio, que Rockstar tiene previsto lanzar la versión para PC de 'GTA VI' durante el primer trimestre de 2027. Todas las fuentes solicitaron permanecer en el anonimato para evitar perjudicar sus relaciones comerciales".
El historial contradice un adelanto. La excepción suele confirmar la regla, aunque la estrategia habitual acostumbra a tener mucho peso en empresas tan gigantescas como Rockstar. Esta siempre ha priorizado las consolas frente al PC. Mientras el estudio no suele dar fechas oficiales, las adaptaciones a ordenador suelen retrasarse un año (o más) con respecto al lanzamiento de consola.

Un beau programme sur le papier, piloté par le showrunner Terry Matalas (qui avait déjà sauvé les meubles sur la saison 3 de Star Trek: Picard en recyclant des décennies de mythologie), avec Paul Bettany de retour dans le rôle de Vision. Malheureusement, entre une écriture boursouflée de jargon informatique et la sacro-sainte obligation d’inclure une grosse baston à effets spéciaux par épisode, la mayonnaise a du mal à prendre.

Pour tenter de combler le vide mémoriel qui le hante, notre androïde se retire régulièrement dans les tréfonds de sa propre psyché.
Cette psyché a de la gueule. Elle prend la forme d’une vaste maison de style victorien où cohabitent les différentes intelligences artificielles conçues par Tony Stark au fil des ans, transformées ici en avatars humains. articles.title: The Blind Spots of Agentic Pentesting and How to Close Them
articles.summary:
By Sila Ozeren Hacioglu, Security Research Engineer at Picus Security.
For years, security teams had a window of several weeks between a CVE going public and attackers exploiting it. Every year, that window got smaller. Then Mythos-class models arrived, and attackers can now weaponize a new CVE within hours. That leaves security teams very little time to find out whether they’re exposed.
That’s where offensive testing comes in. But it has traditionally run on a schedule. Over the years, that schedule got tighter. Annual pentests became quarterly, and automated penetration testing tools made weekly testing possible.
Each advancement shortened the time a change could go untested. Traditional automated pentesting worked fine back when exploitation took weeks. Now that attackers have made a big jump, offensive testing is making one too.
That jump is agentic pentesting. It’s the sharp edge of offensive testing today, but it has blind spots. This piece looks at where they are and how to close them.
How Agentic Pentesting Should Work
A manual pentest usually goes through several phases: reconnaissance, vulnerability assessment, initial access, post-exploitation, and reporting. Traditional automated pentesting tools follow the same phases. Even before LLMs took off, some advanced tools used machine learning to choose the next step. For example, five years ago, we built our Attack Path Validation (APV) product with such a decision engine. But AI agents take it further.

No obstante, muchos prefieren mantener su información privada y no compartir su número o cuenta con terceros.
Cualquiera que sea el caso, ahora podrán unirse a una llamada a través de un enlace. Las personas que se unen como invitados requerirán la aprobación del organizador, por lo que al tocar el enlace compartido serán redirigidas a una sala de espera hasta que se les autorice. articles.title: Electric vehicle sales in the US are showing signs of life | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Don’t go writing the obituary for the U.S. electric vehicle just yet. After sales tanked following the cancellation of tax credits last year, they’ve been growing for the last three consecutive quarters, according to a new report from Cox Automotive.
EVs captured 6.1% of the U.S. market, their best showing since the third quarter of 2025. The data shows that the EV market is “finding its footing again,” Stephanie Valdez Streaty, director of industry insights at Cox Automotive, said in an analysis that accompanied the new report. EV prices have become more competitive, and high gas prices have sparked renewed consumer interest, she added.
Toyota, Rivian, and Subaru led the pack. Sales of the Toyota bZ and Lexus RZ about doubled following a refresh that hit dealerships late last year. The updated models adopted Tesla-style charging ports and received larger batteries, more powerful motors, and faster charging times.
Meanwhile, Tesla’s sales dropped by 20% year-over-year. Tesla still retains the first-mover advantage, though, selling over half of all EVs during the third quarter.
The recovery in the U.S. mimics what occurred in Germany after the government stopped incentives for EV purchases in November 2023, a year earlier than expected. The following month, sales fell by more than half. But after hitting that low, the market steadily recovered. German EV sales in August, the most recent month for which data is available, were the second highest on record.

articles.title: Legendary FPS level designer Richard "Levelord" Gray dies at 68

Prolific first-person shooter level designer Richard “Levelord” Gray died Monday at the age of 68, based on reports shared on social media by Apogee Entertainment yesterday. He had “dealt with cancer on and off for a while now,” according to former colleague Joe Siegler.
After studying computer engineering in the ’80s and tinkering on some early games in COBOL, Gray broke into the industry at the age of 35 in 1994 with the launch of GrayDoom, a set of four maps for the then-new Doom that were widely shared on CompuServe and beyond. The work attracted the attention of Q Studios’ Nick Newhard, who contracted Gray to work on level design for the late ’90s cult classic Blood.
Gray was subsequently hired by 3D Realms, where he said he was given free rein in designing “half the levels” for Duke Nukem 3D. There, he was also responsible for the famous, signed “You’re Not Supposed to Be Here” easter egg, which players could find only by using cheats to explore outside of the usual confines of the map.
Gray said in a 2016 interview that he assumed the prevalence of cheats in Duke Nukem 3D would mean that “of course, most all of you would be flying around, seeing what you could break, find easter eggs the easy way …bingo! I gave you an easter egg that you had to cheat to find.”

Langley told Loizos that the company would end a relationship with a customer where there was clear widespread abuse of its systems. But, the CEO said, it has not to date “fired” a customer, as he put it, such as a police department or law enforcement agency. Langley said Flock had the debate internally, but argued that the company should not take away its product from a community that might need it in its efforts to fight crime.

The cuts equate to roughly 1,000 jobs, and mostly affect those in product, legal, tech, and human resources divisions. According to The Wall Street Journal, the round of layoffs is the company's largest since 2022.
Netflix's struggles aren't new, nor have they gone unaddressed. The streaming giant has explored multiple strategies as of late to boost engagement, with varying degrees of success.
Earlier this year, Netflix launched a kid-friendly gaming app called Playground. In July, they celebrated 10 years of Stranger Things with VHS-style tribute to the series. The streaming giant is also said to be considering a free, ad-supported tier for those unwilling to pay increasingly more expensive monthly fees.
Credit: App Economy Insights
Other initiatives have seen a quicker payoff. Last month, for example, Netflix partnered with Rockstar to host a highly anticipated extended look at Grand Theft Auto VI. Brasil registrou queda de 11% nas remessas no primeiro semestre. Crise das memórias encarece aparelhos.
As remessas globais de smartphones despencaram 20% no terceiro trimestre de 2026 em comparação com o mesmo período de 2025, segundo estimativas da Counterpoint Research. O volume foi o menor registrado para um terceiro trimestre desde 2012, em meio à escassez de memórias e ao encarecimento dos aparelhos.
O levantamento considera os dispositivos enviados pelas fabricantes às lojas e distribuidores. Portanto, os números medem o abastecimento dos canais de venda, e não diretamente as compras feitas pelos consumidores.
A Counterpoint atribui o recuo à alta dos preços das memórias RAM e de armazenamento. Esse encarecimento elevou os custos de fabricação, reduziu a oferta e levou as marcas a repassar parte da conta ao bolso dos compradores.
Segundo a consultoria, os preços dos smartphones no varejo global subiram cerca de 20% em 2026. Os consumidores estão demorando mais para trocar de aparelho e considerando modelos recondicionados, enquanto as fabricantes ajustam seus catálogos para preservar a rentabilidade.
Essa queda já aparecia no trimestre anterior. As remessas globais haviam recuado 11% entre abril e junho, na comparação anual, atingindo o menor volume para um segundo trimestre desde 2013.

Rien n’oblige aujourd’hui un constructeur à installer un autoradio dans une voiture neuve vendue en France. Une directive européenne de 2018 sur les communications électroniques, transposée en 2021, impose seulement que l’autoradio, s’il y en a un, capte le DAB+, la radio numérique terrestre. Une voiture peut donc se contenter d’un système multimédia connecté, et l’écoute de la radio dépend alors entièrement d’une connexion internet. Les sénateurs veulent combler ce vide et ont adopté en première lecture, mardi 13 octobre, la proposition de loi relative à la modernisation de la radio, portée par le sénateur centriste Laurent Lafon et soutenue par le gouvernement.
Le texte répond à un appel lancé fin septembre par Radio France, l’Alliance de la radio, qui réunit les radios privées, et les radios associatives. « Plusieurs constructeurs commercialisent aujourd’hui des véhicules dépourvus de récepteur FM et DAB+, ou proposent la radio en option payante », déploraient-elles dans un communiqué commun. L’enjeu est de taille pour le secteur : d’après le rapport du Sénat, 35 % de l’écoute de la radio se fait en voiture, alors que l’audience a reculé de 18 % entre 2015 et 2025.

articles.title: Colossal Biosciences announces new AI platform to help accelerate de-extinction efforts | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Colossal Biosciences announced Wednesday a new AI platform to help accelerate its efforts to bring back extinct species, TechCrunch can exclusively report.
The platform, called GenoMorph, uses advanced 3D morphology, comparative genomics, and developmental biology to identify genes that could be edited in de-extinction projects with limited gene data. The company is using it as part of its effort to bring back the dodo bird, for which there are limited genomes to work with.
For example, the company is working with only one dodo genome compared to the 100 genomes it has been able to obtain as part of its woolly mammoth de-extinction project. DNA from the woolly mammoth is more plentiful because the colder climates the animal lived in preserve the DNA better than the tropics where the dodo lived, the company said.
“Normally, scientists can compare many genomes to understand which genetic differences are responsible for certain traits,” Colossal CEO and co-founder Ben Lamm told TechCrunch. “We don’t have that luxury with ancient DNA from extinct species whose DNA is severely limited, and we can only get a small number of complete genomes.”
To build GenoMorph, Lamm said the company collected a bunch of developmental data from “chickens, quail, ducks, and pigeons,” and combined it with the “genetic information and 3D skull measurements from more than 70 bird species.” He said it took more than a year of work to build this platform, which also builds on the company’s years of work …

articles.title: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room

articles.title: Cisco patches new Secure Email Gateway zero-day exploited in attacks
articles.summary:
Cisco has patched another actively exploited zero-day flaw in its Secure Email Gateway (SEG) that lets remote unauthenticated attackers execute commands with root privileges.
Tracked as CVE-2026-76519, this vulnerability stems from a relative path traversal weakness in SEG's Advanced Malware Protection (AMP) feature, caused by improper handling of email attachments. Threat actors can exploit this issue by sending an email with a maliciously crafted attachment through an unpatched device.
"A successful exploit could allow the attacker to write arbitrary files and execute commands with root privileges on the underlying operating system," Cisco said in a Wednesday advisory. "In October 2026, the Cisco PSIRT became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability."
CVE-2026-76519 affects SEG instances where the File Reputation service is enabled and assigned to a mail policy, and the Content Scanner Tools version is earlier than 25.3.0.5525.
To determine whether a specific device is vulnerable, admins have to use the contentscannerstatus CLI command to check what version of Content Scanner Tools is running and inspect the "Enable File Reputation" checkbox under Mail Policies > Incoming Mail Policies > Advanced Malware Protection or Mail Policies > Outgoing Mail Policies > Advanced Malware Protection in the web-based management interface.

A design engineer specifying a compact industrial panel reaches for a Class CC fuse holder. It’s UL Listed under File No. E359089, rated 600V AC/DC, and built with a rejection feature that physically stops a lower-rated fuse from ever being substituted in the field. articles.title: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
articles.summary:
A protein is a chain of amino acids held together by what are called peptide bonds. On their own, those bonds are extremely stable; they’re estimated to have a half-life of several hundred years. But in Earth’s environment, most proteins don’t last nearly that long. That’s because organisms have evolved a handful of ways to catalyze the break-up of peptide bonds, which have diversified into countless specialized protein-digesting enzymes. Proteases are everywhere and generally make short work of any proteins that find their way into the environment.
Now, researchers have basically short-circuited the diversification process, using AI-based protein design tools to take the catalytic core of two types of protease and replace the entire rest of the protein. The resulting enzymes could be tuned to cut specific proteins in half, and the researchers demonstrated their effectiveness by using them to cut proteins associated with neurological diseases.
Cutting proteins
The basic peptide bond isn’t especially interesting-looking—it’s what you get when you link an amino group to an acid, releasing a water molecule in the process. As their name implies, amino acids have both an amino and an acid group, allowing them to form peptide bonds on two sides of the amino acid. This is critical for building up the long chains found in proteins. (The amino acids also have side chains with distinctive chemistry, which gives a backbone specific properties.)

articles.title: SolarWinds' Avior pairs AI agents with deterministic execution for enterprise IT - SiliconANGLE

SolarWinds’ Avior pairs AI agents with deterministic execution for enterprise IT
Observability and information technology management software company SolarWinds Worldwide LLC today unveiled Avior, a standalone agentic artificial intelligence system built to take on first-line operations work for enterprise IT teams.
The launch goes after the reliability problem that comes with letting AI agents act on production systems. SolarWinds argues that an agent producing different outcomes from one run to the next is a liability wherever uptime and security are on the line. Most IT organizations already absorb that cost in outage time and audit exposure, the company said.
Chief Technology Officer Krishna Sai said the design grounds “probabilistic models in deterministic execution.” The models work out what needs doing. Ledger is asking resellers and distributors in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong to halt wallet sales and remove products from shelves while it investigates hardware implant incidents.
The company announced the decision in response to discovering that devices purchased from CryptoBilis had been modified to steal seed phrases used to access crypto assets and send them to an unauthorized party over an LTE connection.
Ledger sells physical cryptocurrency wallets that securely store private keys used for managing and authorizing digital asset transactions.
Following reports of cryptocurrency losses from multiple users, Ledger launched an investigation on October 9 and confirmed that some devices sold by CryptoBilis had been tampered with.
Yesterday, Ledger’s Donjon security arm shared more details about the hardware implant found inside devices from the reseller , largely confirming earlier reports by Mark Karpelès and Tibane Labs.
Donjon said the implant’s microcontroller detects and decodes the 24-word recovery phrase for setting up and restoring the wallet, then transmits it over LTE using a provisioned eSIM.
The implant is a separate component that does not modify the Secure Element or Ledger operating system, or alter transactions or signatures, which makes it undetectable by Ledger’s integrity self-checks.

SK hynix has detailed plans to reduce reliance on power-hungry CPU cores with an in-house core named a Hynix Transaction Processing Unit (H-TPU). Not to be confused with an AI accelerator, an H-TPU would assist with repetitive work handled by an SSD, which usually demands more cores on a controller as drives get faster. These new cores are placed in clusters and would handle routine I/O with a four-stage, in-order pipeline, while management is left to the traditional Arm CPU. Lewis found it difficult to finish the book, however, writing four other Narnia books first before completing The Magician’s Nephew in 1955.
There have been several adaptations, in various media, of The Chronicles of Narnia, most recently the early 2000s film franchise adapting the first three novels in the series. AI infrastructure networking is approaching a physical turning point as the copper links that tie GPUs together inside a rack strain under ever-faster signaling speeds. The move to light-based interconnects could redraw the boundaries of what counts as a single AI system.
Cisco Systems Inc. is pressing that transition on several fronts, from new silicon and pluggable optics to an optical standard being developed with Nvidia Corp. The industry now sits at the pivot point between electrical and optical interconnects, according to Rakesh Chopra (pictured), senior vice president of silicon and systems architecture and Cisco fellow at Cisco.
“Right now, in-rack copper, in-system copper … is not a durable place to stand,” Chopra said. “It will switch to optical. My guess is what you’ll see is in a handful of years, that’ll be the norm, and that allows you to take your scale-up domain from a single rack to row-scale or beyond.”
Chopra spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier at the AI Data Pipeline Forum, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI infrastructure networking, the limits of copper interconnects and the shift to denser optical modules. (* Disclosure below.)

articles.title: CedarDB wants one database to handle both transactions and analytics, as AI agents raise the stakes | TechCrunch

Databases have traditionally been built for one of two jobs. Analytical databases help businesses spot trends and answer questions, while operational databases store the day-to-day records of transactions, like orders and payments. But the Munich-based database engine CedarDB supports both, and its approach has gained relevance with the rise of agentic AI, its cofounder and CEO Moritz Sichert told TechCrunch.
CedarDB has been in the making for the last decade, but its current momentum stems from enterprise companies whose existing data stacks may have been well suited to storing years of transactions, yet less suited to quickly answering analytical questions asked in natural language about that data.
CedarDB’s questioning of the divide between analytical and operational queries is a byproduct of its focus on efficiency. The company is a Technical University of Munich spinout based on Umbra, a research project that was built from scratch to beat legacy database engines at processing speed by making the most of modern hardware.
With five Umbra researchers as its cofounders, CedarDB kept that approach, promising faster performance without requiring more CPUs or processing power and memory — and requiring few changes from customers. ScaleFlux bets smarter SSD controllers can break the AI memory bottleneck
AI factories run on graphics processing units that cost a fortune and work at blistering speed, yet those chips increasingly sit idle waiting for data. As the bottleneck moves from compute to memory and storage, NAND flash is being asked to do far more than hold files.
That shift is putting data movement constraints at the center of AI infrastructure planning. A GPU operates at about 20 to 22 terabytes per second, and every tier of the hierarchy below it adds delay, according to Pichai Balaji (pictured), vice president of products and marketing at ScaleFlux Inc.
“When you move to DRAM, it is almost 37 to 40 times slower than what the GPU wants. You go even further down to the storage side, it is almost 800 times slower,” Balaji said. “A bottleneck is created all throughout when the data is moving from the GPU into the memory, into the storage. The bottleneck just gets amplified.”
Balaji spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier at the AI Data Pipeline Forum, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed AI factories, smarter controllers and using NAND flash as active memory for AI workloads. (* Disclosure below.)

Certains s’apprêtaient à changer de matériel, à tort. La mise à jour KB5127648, diffusée le 13 octobre pour les versions 24H2 à 26H2 de Windows 11, règle la question en une ligne : le problème venait du système.
« Cette mise à jour corrige un problème qui pouvait provoquer des saccades de la souris dans certains jeux », indique une seule ligne des notes officielles, glissée dans la rubrique jeux sans autre forme d’annonce. Le dysfonctionnement touchait la gestion des entrées de la souris par le système, avec des à-coups visibles dans plusieurs titres en ligne. L’installation passe par Windows Update, avec la mise à jour cumulative d’octobre. Les joueurs qui avaient suspendu leurs mises à jour devront donc les relancer pour en profiter.

Vast Data bets stitched-together AI pipelines can’t keep sensitive data in sync
Data sovereignty is becoming an architectural problem as enterprises push artificial intelligence inference toward their most sensitive information. Pipelines assembled from separate tools struggle to keep embeddings, permissions and source data aligned, leaving many valuable data sets out of AI’s reach.
The shift from model training to inference is changing what AI infrastructure has to deliver, and it has fueled demand for Vast Data Inc., which raised about $1 billion at a $30 billion valuation in April 2026. Platforms built for scale and speed now must also handle user identification, access control and regulated data, according to Vaughn Stewart (pictured), vice president of systems engineering at Vast.
“There’s kind of different philosophical concepts in the market, right? One is the bespoke model … a best-in-breed of every piece in an agentic pipeline,” Stewart said. “And what we see there is just too much exposure to having data that’s maybe not in sync between being updated versus the vector embeddings, or maybe not in sync between the user access controls on the source data versus what’s provided through an inference query.”

Y los estudios tampoco terminan de ponerse de acuerdo, igual que los informes energéticos.
La paradoja nuclear. Un análisis reciente disecciona este problema comparando las previsiones de los años 70 con la potencia atómica instalada actualmente. Y la generación eléctrica continúa creciendo.

From loans to dependants and future goals, calculating term insurance cover shows a protection gap of Rs 1.2 crore — and why young professionals need to look beyond salary multiples.
Many young professionals assume their existing cover is sufficient. However, the question they need to ask is ‘how much term insurance do I need’, to adequately protect their family from outstanding liabilities and future financial goals.
A life cover of Rs 50 lakh can sound substantial at 28. You may have just received an appraisal, begun an SIP, and perhaps taken a home loan with the confidence that your career is still on an upward curve. But life cover is not meant to reflect where your income stands today alone. It needs to account for the financial responsibilities your family would have to manage if your income stopped unexpectedly.
Consider a 28-year-old startup employee earning Rs 15 lakh a year. He has Rs 50 lakh of existing cover: Rs 20 lakh through his employer and a Rs 30 lakh individual policy. On paper, he is insured. In reality, he could still have a protection gap of Rs 1.2 crore.
Why existing cover can create false comfort

London-based offensive security startup CodeWall Ltd. officially launched today with $4 million in new funding to give enterprises such as banks autonomous artificial intelligence agents that attack them the way an outside hacker would.
CodeWall begins each engagement with no credentials or inside knowledge of the target. Several agents, each built for a different kind of job, work on it at the same time. According to the company, whatever one of them finds is logged to a common investigation graph, so a weak spot in a single application can become another agent’s route into connected systems and data.
Customers see each completed attack path step by step, with the evidence attached. The agents go back in whenever new systems come online or a fix is applied, and they keep to whatever scope the customer has authorized. Founder and Chief Executive Paul Price calls that ongoing testing “a permanent capability,” and CodeWall is pitching the service as a replacement for the penetration tests most enterprises commission once or twice a year.
Earlier this year CodeWall turned its agents on the Big Three management consulting firms. At McKinsey & Co. Head of Security at Opera.
That gap was easier to overlook when browsers had a relatively simple job. They opened websites and displayed them on a screen. But today, browsers hold login credentials, manage permissions, block trackers and increasingly give AI agents the ability to act on a user's behalf. The browser has gone from being a window on the internet to one of the most important layers between people and everything they do online.
That shift is understandably enough to make users more cautious than they used to be when online. But, misunderstandings about browsers means that caution may be misdirected. Many users make decisions about tools based on outdated assumptions, shaping everything. Users make very different from what they install to what they let an AI feature access.

Rockstar Expects Faster Development For Games After GTA 6
Rockstar's next game after GTA 6 probably won't take another eight years to make, at least according to the studio's own leadership. In a making-of feature on Grand Theft Auto 6 by Bloomberg, heads of development Phil Hooker and Aaron Garbut explained that the engine, tools, and team built during the game's long development will let Rockstar move faster on future projects. Hooker said he feels confident the studio can now build on top of that groundwork instead of rebuilding it for every new game. Garbut added that a lot was changed at a foundational level for GTA 6, "but now it's done, and we're not going to rip it apart."
The pair pointed to GTA 3 and Vice City as the model here, with Vice City arriving roughly a year after GTA 3 since it was built on work that was already done. That's a very different picture from today, with GTA 6 having gone through roughly eight years of full development. The game is now set to launch on November 19, 2026 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S after being initially delayed to May 2026 and then pushed again to November. Apparently, Rockstar has also grown to more than 4,700 employees across 12 offices. Rockstar hasn't revealed what it's working on next, and neither Hooker nor Garbut put a timeline on it. It's reasonable to expect a shorter wait than the 13 years between GTA 5 and GTA 6, though how much shorter is anyone's guess for now.

articles.summary:
Uvi raises $7.5M to help AI agents learn business context and run at eight times lower cost
Agentic artificial intelligence startup Uvi said today it has raised $7.5 million in seed funding to tackle an expensive problem around business context that’s draining millions of dollars annually from the coffers of enterprises using autonomous AI agents.
It’s backed by CT Innovations, which led the round, alongside Cardumen, Mana VC and 91 Ventures, which joined as participating investors.
Each time a new AI agent is deployed, it knows nothing at all about the company that deployed it. Those agents have to learn everything about the company’s business processes and operations from scratch in a process that’s repeated again and again, racking up significant costs in terms of computing resources.
Business context is crucial to agentic operations. If an AI agent is going to be able to work autonomously for an organization without constant human oversight, it needs to be well versed in the way that company operates.

Edge security startup Huskeys Security Ltd. today added Profiling to its platform to map out which parts of a company’s web applications the business depends on.
The new capability goes after a longstanding problem at the network edge, where most large organizations run a stack of third-party security products from different vendors. Content delivery networks, bot defenses and web application firewalls each see only their own layer of traffic. Without context from the others, Huskeys argues, controls tend to end up generic, and that can mean blocking legitimate customers.
Profiling starts with the application itself. The software looks at who is calling each endpoint and what those callers, human or automated, appear to be after. The paths most important to the business get marked, as do the security controls already in place. With that profile in hand, Huskeys can judge each request by the standards of the customer’s own application.
Huskeys’ co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Roy Weisfeld said most organizations protect everything the same way, “like a mall with one security team guarding every store identically, whether it’s a luxury boutique or a snack stand.” Profiling is meant to give each store its own guard, he added.

articles.title: En 1945 la bomba nuclear se hizo realidad: acto seguido imaginamos los proyectos atómicos más locos posibles
articles.summary:
En los años cincuenta parecía que la humanidad estaba a las puertas de una nueva revolución industrial. La energía atómica iba a dejar atrás el carbón, el petróleo y el vapor que heredamos de la primera. No todo era de color de rosa, claro, pero la inocencia de la época, y lo poco que se sabía entonces de los peligros de la radiación, nos dejó algunos proyectos tan ambiciosos como disparatados. Ninguno pasó de prototipo.
Hoy la energía nuclear produce electricidad en todo el mundo y mueve submarinos, portaaviones y rompehielos. En aquella época, sin embargo, se llegó a pensar que el átomo podía moverlo absolutamente todo.
El principio es sencillo. Cuando el núcleo de un átomo pesado, como el uranio o el plutonio, se divide, libera una enorme cantidad de energía en forma de radiación y de calor. Si esa reacción en cadena se descontrola, tenemos una bomba. Si se modera, tenemos un reactor que calienta agua hasta convertirla en vapor y mueve una turbina, como en cualquier central nuclear. Con esa idea en la cabeza, ingenieros de coches, aviones y naves espaciales se pusieron a soñar.
En 1958 Ford presentó el Nucleon, un coche concepto propulsado por un pequeño reactor colocado entre las ruedas traseras. El reactor generaría vapor para mover unas turbinas, y la cabina iba muy adelantada para alejar a los ocupantes del núcleo. articles.title: Beyond Lithography: 3D Scaling Puts New Demands on Materials - EE Times
articles.summary:
For decades, semiconductor scaling has been described largely in terms of shrinking dimensions. But as logic and memory structures increasingly extend vertically as well as laterally, printing smaller features is only part of the manufacturing challenge.
“The challenge rotates now,” Stephen Sopko, semiconductor and deep-tech practice lead at HyperFRAME Research, told EE Times. Instead of thinking primarily about patterning structures from above, manufacturers increasingly have to grow, etch, and fill them in three dimensions, controlling materials on surfaces that may be buried within increasingly complex devices.
Lithography remains essential. Sopko described it as “setting the pitch and the critical dimension.” But once those increasingly small dimensions have been defined, deposition, etch, and materials engineering play growing roles in determining whether the resulting structures can actually be manufactured at scale.
That transition is creating opportunities for semiconductor equipment companies to rethink materials that have performed relatively straightforward jobs for decades.
ASM International is targeting one of those opportunities with Flowable Carbon, its plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) technology designed to fill complex 3D structures while creating a planar surface. The company said the technology can, in some process flows, eliminate subsequent chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) and etch-back steps.

Una reducción de hasta el 30% en el consumo energético del refrigerador depende de una tarea de mantenimiento: impedir que se acumule escarcha. El hielo en las paredes internas obliga al electrodoméstico a usar más energía para mantener la temperatura, un gasto que se traslada a la factura de electricidad.
La ubicación del aparato, el estado de la puerta, el orden de los alimentos y la temperatura elegida inciden en el funcionamiento. Según pautas de Endesa, una serie de hábitos domésticos permite conservar los productos en condiciones adecuadas sin exigir de más al compresor.
Cuál es el mejor lugar para ubicar el refrigerador
El aparato debe ubicarse en un sector fresco, ventilado y alejado de fuentes de calor. Colocarlo junto al horno, una cocina, un radiador o una ventana con sol directo hará que el compresor necesite más energía para sostener la temperatura interna.
Además, es necesario dejar cerca de 10 centímetros de distancia entre la parte trasera del refrigerador y la pared. Ese espacio permite la circulación del aire alrededor del electrodoméstico y favorece la disipación del calor. Si el aparato queda muy pegado al muro, el sistema pierde capacidad para liberar la temperatura que extrae del interior.

Débrancher sa box et la rebrancher aussitôt ne sert quasiment à rien. La raison tient en un mot : condensateurs. Ces minuscules composants stockent de l'énergie résiduelle après la coupure, et tant qu'ils ne sont pas vidés, la mémoire du routeur conserve ses bugs intacts.
Le réflexe est universel. Le Wi-Fi rame, on arrache la prise, on rebranche dans la foulée, et on attend le miracle. Sauf que ce geste expéditif rate l'essentiel du processus de remise à zéro. La carte mère de votre routeur embarque des condensateurs, de minuscules composants qui stockent de l'énergie résiduelle après la coupure d'alimentation. Tant qu'ils ne sont pas complètement déchargés, les puces mémoire conservent une partie de leur état précédent, bugs compris.
Ce qui se passe vraiment pendant ces 30 secondes
Quand vous débranchez votre routeur, le voyant lumineux reste allumé une ou deux secondes. C'est l'énergie des condensateurs qui s'écoule. Sur la plupart des équipements réseau grand public, la décharge complète prend entre 10 et 30 secondes. Ce délai permet à la mémoire vive de se vider intégralement.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches Record 1,413 Flaws, Including Exploited Windows Shell Bug
articles.summary:
Microsoft on Tuesday shattered its own Patch Tuesday record by shipping patches for a whopping 1,413 vulnerabilities, including one that it said has come under active exploitation.
These include 1,102 flaws in Windows, 134 in Office, 61 in Developer Tools, 36 in SharePoint Server, and 22 in SQL Server. Of these, more than 670 relate to privilege escalation, followed by over 300 remote code execution flaws and 250 information disclosure flaws. Over 70 flaws are rated Critical in severity.
"Hundreds of CVEs in a single release used to be the exception; now it's the baseline," Dustin Childs, head of Threat Awareness at the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), said. "Is AI to blame? Partly. It's accelerating bug-hunting on both sides of the fence, so vendors are finding (and fixing) more flaws, and researchers are finding them faster too."
"But AI isn't creating these bugs out of thin air; it's just shortening the time between a vulnerability existing and someone noticing it. The volume isn't the real story anymore. What matters is that discovery is scaling faster than exploitation, so teams that triage by sheer CVE count instead of exploitability are burning cycles on the wrong bugs. Patch what's proven, prioritized, and public, and treat everything else as this month's new normal."

articles.title: Four-Byte Write and Timing Bug Let Researchers Run Code in Windows SmartScreen Enclave
articles.summary:
Security researchers ran their own code inside a protected part of Windows that is meant to stay sealed off even when the rest of the computer is taken over.
The protected area is a VBS enclave, an isolated slice of memory the operating system uses to guard secrets, and the one they broke into handles passwords for a Windows anti-phishing feature.
The work was done in a lab as a proof of concept, has not been seen in real attacks, and Microsoft fixed the flaw in its September 8, 2026 update.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-83498. Microsoft rates it an elevation-of-privilege issue, Critical, with a CVSS score of 7.8, and says it has not been exploited and was not publicly known before the fix. Microsoft also says it found the same issue internally. The research, by the security firm Doyensec, was published October 13, more than a month after the patch.
A VBS enclave is a signed library that a normal Windows program loads but cannot read or change once it is running. The Windows hypervisor keeps the enclave's memory in a more trusted world, called VTL1 or Isolated User Mode, that ordinary code in the normal world, VTL0, cannot reach, according to Microsoft.
The design is meant to protect what is inside even if an attacker has already taken over the normal kernel or is running as SYSTEM. Running attacker-chosen code inside that world is what makes this research notable.

articles.title: “Este número de teléfono no puede usar WhatsApp”: qué hacer si aparece este error al abrir la app

El mensaje señala que la cuenta vinculada a esa línea fue suspendida y que, en ciertos casos, existe una fase para solicitar una revisión.

Por qué aparece la alerta de que una cuenta no puede usar WhatsApp
La suspensión pasa cuando WhatsApp considera que una cuenta incumplió sus condiciones del servicio. Entre los motivos que señala la plataforma están el envío de spam, posibles fraudes y conductas que puedan afectar la seguridad de otros usuarios.

articles.title: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
articles.summary:
A flaw in Linux's vhost subsystem lets a local user read and write kernel memory at will and become root across nearly a decade of kernel versions. In one virtualization setup, it lets an untrusted virtual machine write to the host's memory and hijack the program that runs the virtual machine.
The bug is tracked as CVE-2026-74580 and named Vghost. Tencent Zhuque Lab, which found the flaw, released a fix on August 3 and published a full write-up on October 12 with working demos of both attacks. There is no public sign it has been exploited yet.
vhost is the part of the Linux kernel that speeds up network and other input/output for virtual machines and containers. A local user reaches it by opening a device node, usually /dev/vhost-net or /dev/vhost-vsock.
On the host, the flaw gives an unprivileged user a reliable way to read and write any kernel address, bypass KASLR, and escalate to root. The attack is deterministic: it needs no memory grooming and no lucky timing.
The second attack is narrower. When a virtual machine's virtio device is placed behind a virtual IOMMU with iommu_platform turned on, and vhost runs in device-IOTLB mode, an untrusted guest can trigger the same bug and make the host kernel write out of bounds into the host's QEMU process. From there, a guest can overwrite a function pointer in QEMU and take control of where the host process runs next, or crash it.

RDNA 5 lancé en fin d'année 2027 ?
Cela n'aura échappé à personne, AMD se montre plutôt discret quant au futur de sa gamme Radeon et, en particulier, à sa prochaine génération de GPU, basée sur l'architecture RDNA 5.
Pourtant, d'après les dernières informations relayées par le site Wccftech, il se pourrait que l'architecture RDNA 5 fasse ses débuts commerciaux bien plus tôt que nous ne le pensions, dans la seconde moitié de 2027. Une estimation que nos confrères ne sortent pas du chapeau et qui vient d'un informateur plutôt fiable dans le secteur, Kepler_L2. Ce dernier ne donne évidemment pas ses sources, mais parle de cette rumeur dans les forums d'AnandTech.
Si un tel calendrier vient à se confirmer, on pourrait donc avoir un premier rendez-vous avec RDNA 5 dès le Computex 2027, lequel se tiendra à Taipei du 1ᵉʳ au 4 juin 2027. articles.title: An AI Agent Found a Critical OTP Bypass in Production. The Attack Was the Easy Part.
articles.summary:
The bug was simple: the login let you choose where your sign-in code went. Proving it on a live website was the hard part.
TL;DR
- During an authorized assessment, an AI pentesting agent found a critical authentication bypass on a major insurer's production website, on its own.
- One login request let the user choose where the one-time passcode went.
- The attack was the easy part. Proving it on a live site took web context built over a decade.
The Login Worked. Then the Agent Stopped.
Reflectiz's AI pentesting agent was mapping the login flow of a major insurer's production website, which has millions of users.
The agent requested a login code and directed it to an email inbox it controlled. The code arrived. The login went through. Its guardrails halted the test after the login succeeded.
The agent had discovered a critical-severity authentication bypass on its own. Reflectiz reported it to the insurer.
The Flaw: The Request Chose Where the Code Went
A one-time passcode (OTP) only proves who you are if it goes somewhere already linked to the account. Here, that link was broken.
The login request carried two fields that decided delivery: the channel and the address. Normally, the code went by text to the phone number on the account. But the request could change the channel. Switch it to email, and the server sent the code to whatever address the request named, not the address registered to the account.

articles.title: Researchers Used a Public OpenAI Model to Build a $250,000 Chrome Full-Chain Exploit in Six Days
articles.summary:
A team at security firm XBOW chained three then-unknown Google Chrome bugs into a single attack that runs code on a Windows computer when the user only loads a web page, the company said.
Its researchers built the attack in six days by directing AI agents running OpenAI's publicly available GPT-5.6 Sol model. Google has since confirmed all three bugs, fixed them, and paid XBOW its top $250,000 reward for a full Chrome exploit.
The attack is a full chain: a set of bugs used together to break every layer of Chrome's protection, from a web page all the way to the computer.
Chrome runs web page code inside two nested sandboxes, the barriers that stop a hacked page from reaching the rest of the machine. The chain crossed both. The result was code running outside Chrome on Windows, with no need for the user to click or download anything.
All three bugs are now fixed, and XBOW says they were never used against Chrome users. The two that carry public identifiers were fixed in Chrome 152.0.7977.65 on August 25 and 152.0.7977.82 on September 3.
Chrome updates on its own, but the fix only takes effect after the browser restarts, so the action is to relaunch Chrome and confirm the version is 152.0.7977.82 or later.

She's traveling, she's rushed, and she apologizes for the bad connection. Ten minutes later an email lands with the wire details.
A couple of years ago that scenario was a conference talk. Now it shows up in incident reports. In a 2025 Gartner survey of 302 cybersecurity leaders, 62% said their organization had experienced at least one deepfake attack in the prior 12 months. In the same survey, 43% reported at least one deepfake audio call incident and 37% had run into deepfakes on video calls.
And the wire is only the obvious ask. The same cloned voice can call the help desk to move an MFA token, or ask an identity admin to set up a new global admin ahead of an "audit." A fraudulent wire tends to surface at reconciliation. A quietly added admin account can sit there for months.
Most organizations have a policy that says to verify unusual payment and access requests. articles.title: curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code Execution
articles.summary:
A flaw in how curl handles HTTP/2 uploads lets a malicious server receiving an upload corrupt the client's memory, and the researcher who reported it turned that into code execution on the uploading machine.
The curl project fixed it on October 14 in curl 8.23.0. Taking over a client needs exact knowledge of its build and memory layout, and curl expects a real attack to end in a crash instead.
The flaw, a use-after-free tracked as CVE-2026-92392, affects curl and libcurl 8.12.0 through 8.22.0, both the command-line tool and the library that many other programs use for transfers. curl rates it High on its own four-level scale, its first High-severity flaw since the SOCKS5 heap overflow of October 2023. The project cut its release cycle by two weeks to ship the fix.
The attack runs from the server side. The client has to upload a file of roughly 135KB over HTTP/2 to a server controlled by the attacker, and the server's certificate must pass the client's checks. libcurl negotiates HTTP/2 by default for https:// URLs when the server offers it, and the library was built with HTTP/2 support.
The flaw has shipped in every curl release since 8.12.0 in February 2025. No source reports attacks that use it. The reporter's HackerOne write-up, with the malicious server script and a Docker container described as reproducing the code execution, became public on October 14 with the advisory.

articles.summary:
Attackers exploited a flaw in an optional Nextcloud app, Collabora Online - Built-in CODE Server, to plant web shells on Nextcloud servers. Three administrators reported the issue on GitHub, with the first logged attack on September 10.
A web shell is a small file that executes any command an attacker sends via a web request, with the rights of the web server account. The flaw allows an unauthenticated request to run a command on the server, but only when the app's local document server is not running, such as during a restart or upgrade, or after a crash.
Collabora fixed it in version 26.4.303 on September 11 and on October 14 published an advisory with the identifier CVE-2026-110447, warning that turning off the app does not help: it must be updated or removed.
Who Is Affected
The app, published by Collabora under the package name richdocumentscode, downloads a copy of Collabora Online Development Edition (CODE) and runs it on the Nextcloud server itself.
That lets Nextcloud Office edit documents without a separate Collabora server. Its store listing says it is "for local testing and non-production use" and "for personal use or for small teams."
Collabora's advisory covers every version before 26.4.303 and says standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected. Según detalló Evans, de la electricidad que se extrae de la red para alimentar estas instalaciones, un máximo del 70% se destina efectivamente al procesamiento de inteligencia artificial. El 30% restante representa ineficiencias que, de acuerdo con la visión de Nvidia, los diseños futuros de centros de datos deberían reducir.
Dónde se pierde la energía en un centro de datos de un gigavatio
Evans desglosó el origen de esas pérdidas. En un centro de datos con capacidad de un gigavatio, el 20% de la energía se pierde en procesos de refrigeración, distribución eléctrica y conversión de potencia. Un 10% adicional se pierde por configuraciones incorrectas de los racks de servidores, además de fallas y reinicios de los sistemas.
“Firmas un contrato por 100 megavatios, pero nunca obtenés realmente esa cifra. Con algo de suerte, conseguirás 93 megavatios, y en ciertos momentos del día, incluso menos”, explicó el directivo de Nvidia. articles.title: Five Practical Limits to Check Before Installing a 3D LED Fan Display - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
A 3D LED fan display can produce an unusual visual effect: an illuminated object appears to float against its surroundings. That can be useful for a product feature or a decorative installation, but the effect should be evaluated in the room where it will actually be used. A demonstration reel is only the beginning of that assessment.
Before choosing a model, work through five practical limits. They concern the environment, the audience, the content, the physical installation and the operating process. None can be settled simply by choosing the largest display or the most elaborate animation.
1. The room is part of the picture
Ambient light and the background influence how clearly an illuminated subject stands out. A visually busy wall, strong reflection or bright window may compete with the animation. Examine the proposed location at the hours you expect to use it, rather than testing only after dark or with the surrounding lights switched off.
The display examples at HologramFans.com can help buyers identify the visual effect they want to investigate. Before selecting a model, check that effect against the actual room, content and manufacturer’s installation requirements.
Use a sample of your own intended content during the demonstration. A clear, isolated object may work differently from a detailed logo or a scene with several elements. Look at the complete installation, including any protective enclosure, before deciding that a promotional recording represents the result …

articles.title: How Technology Is Simplifying Business Relocation and Company Management - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Technology has transformed the way businesses operate, expand, and manage daily activities. Entrepreneurs can now coordinate teams remotely, maintain digital records, automate administrative tasks, and access essential business information from almost anywhere. These capabilities have also made relocating a business more manageable.
However, moving a company to another location involves more than changing an office address. Business owners must consider legal requirements, financial obligations, employee coordination, data security, and operational continuity. Modern technology helps simplify these responsibilities by improving efficiency, reducing manual work, and supporting better decision-making.
1. Digital Tools Are Simplifying Business Relocation
Business relocation often requires multiple tasks to be completed within a specific timeframe. These may include arranging office facilities, updating business records, notifying customers, coordinating suppliers, and managing administrative paperwork.
Digital project management platforms help bring these activities together in one place. Business owners can create task lists, assign responsibilities, establish deadlines, and monitor progress without relying on scattered emails or paper documents.
Centralized Project Management
Project management software provides a clear overview of the relocation process. Team members can track completed tasks, identify outstanding responsibilities, and communicate about potential delays.

articles.title: 7 Best POS Systems in Australia for Small Businesses - Tech Guide
articles.summary:
Square, POSApt, Lightspeed, Shopify POS, Abacus, OrderMate and Zeller are seven of the best POS systems worth considering for Australian small businesses. Each suits a different combination of sales, stock, service and online ordering needs.
Square is a practical starting point for straightforward selling. POSApt is worth considering for businesses seeking Australian support and a website with online ordering and table booking. Lightspeed offers specialised retail and restaurant systems, while Shopify POS connects physical shops with Shopify online stores.
The right choice depends on what happens during a normal working day. A café needs to send customised orders to the correct kitchen printer. A clothing shop needs to track sizes and colours. A restaurant needs to manage tables and split bills without slowing service.
This comparison explains where each system fits, which features matter and what to check before committing. The order is an editorial shortlist, rather than a market-share ranking.
What Should a Small Business Look for in a POS System?
A POS system should help staff complete everyday tasks accurately and give owners useful information about the business.
Before comparing providers, identify your essential workflows:
- Sales: Can staff find products, apply modifiers and process refunds easily?
- Stock: Do you need basic product quantities or purchasing, recipes and ingredient tracking?
- Orders: Must online, takeaway and dine-in orders reach the same system?
